questions.prompt: A company has separate AWS accounts for development and production. Developers in the development account need read-only access to an Amazon S3 bucket in the production account. Which solution meets these requirements MOST securely?
choices: Make the bucket public and restrict access with a bucket policy that checks the developers' IP addresses
Create a read-only IAM role in the production account that trusts the development account
Copy the bucket contents nightly to a bucket in the development account using the production root user's keys
Create IAM users in the production account for each developer and share their access keys through a secure email
questions.explanation: A cross-account IAM role provides temporary credentials scoped to read-only access, avoiding long-term keys and duplicate users.

questions.prompt: An application running on Amazon EC2 instances must write items to an Amazon DynamoDB table. The security team prohibits storing long-term credentials on the instances. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Embed the access keys in the AMI and rotate the AMI every 90 days
Attach an IAM role with the required DynamoDB permissions to the instances through an instance profile
Pass the IAM user's access keys to the instances through EC2 user data at launch
Store an IAM user's access keys in the application configuration file on an encrypted EBS volume
questions.explanation: An instance profile delivers automatically rotated temporary credentials through the instance metadata service, so no long-term keys are stored.

questions.prompt: A company uses AWS Organizations. The security team must ensure that no one in any member account, including administrators, can stop or delete AWS CloudTrail trails. Which solution meets this requirement?
choices: Attach an SCP to the organization root that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail
Create an AWS Config rule that detects when a trail is stopped and sends an SNS notification
Attach an IAM policy to every administrator in each account that denies the CloudTrail actions
Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation and S3 versioning in every member account
questions.explanation: An SCP applies to all principals in member accounts, including administrators and the root user, so the deny cannot be overridden locally. Config only detects the change after it happens.

questions.prompt: A developer in a member account has the AdministratorAccess managed policy attached. A service control policy on the account's OU denies ec2:RunInstances in all Regions except us-east-1. What happens when the developer tries to launch an instance in eu-west-1?
choices: The request succeeds because SCPs apply only to the root user of member accounts
The request is denied because SCPs set the maximum available permissions and the explicit deny applies
The request succeeds because the identity-based AdministratorAccess policy overrides the SCP
The request is denied only if a permissions boundary is also attached to the developer
questions.explanation: SCPs limit the maximum permissions for every principal in a member account; an explicit deny in an SCP cannot be overridden by an IAM policy.

questions.prompt: A company attached a service control policy to the organization root that denies access to a specific AWS service. Users in the management account can still use the service. What is the reason?
choices: Service control policies do not affect users or roles in the management account
Service control policies take up to 24 hours to propagate to the management account
The SCP must also be attached directly to each IAM user in the management account
The management account users have permissions boundaries that override SCPs
questions.explanation: SCPs never restrict the management account, which is one reason AWS recommends keeping workloads out of it.

questions.prompt: A company must prevent resources from being created outside of two approved AWS Regions across all accounts in its organization, while still allowing global services such as IAM. Which approach is MOST effective?
choices: Use AWS Config in every Region to delete any resource created outside the approved Regions
Disable the unapproved Regions in each VPC's route table so that API calls cannot reach them
Create an IAM group in each account with a policy that allows only the approved Regions
Apply an SCP that denies requests whose aws:RequestedRegion is not approved, exempting global services
questions.explanation: An SCP with a deny on aws:RequestedRegion centrally enforces the guardrail for every account, and NotAction exceptions keep global services working.

questions.prompt: A company wants to let developers create IAM roles for their Lambda functions without allowing them to grant those roles more permissions than the developers themselves are allowed. Which IAM feature should be used?
choices: Permissions boundaries that the developers must attach to any role they create
IAM Access Analyzer policy validation that runs before each deployment pipeline
Service control policies attached directly to each developer's IAM user
Resource-based policies attached to each Lambda function
questions.explanation: Requiring a permissions boundary on created roles caps their effective permissions, which safely delegates role creation.

questions.prompt: A company stores sensitive reports in an Amazon S3 bucket. The reports must be accessible only from applications running in a specific VPC. Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: Attach a network ACL to the S3 bucket that allows only the VPC's private subnets
Enable S3 Block Public Access and grant access to the VPC's internet gateway in the bucket policy
Create an S3 gateway endpoint and a bucket policy that denies requests not using it, based on aws:SourceVpce
Create a security group for the bucket that allows inbound traffic only from the VPC CIDR range
questions.explanation: S3 buckets cannot have security groups or NACLs; a bucket policy conditioned on aws:SourceVpce restricts access to the VPC endpoint.

questions.prompt: EC2 instances in a private subnet with no internet access must call AWS Secrets Manager. The traffic must not traverse the public internet. What should a solutions architect configure?
choices: An interface VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager with private DNS enabled
An egress-only internet gateway attached to the VPC
A NAT gateway in a public subnet with a route from the private subnet
A gateway VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager attached to the private route table
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager is reached privately through an interface endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink; gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB.

questions.prompt: A security team detects repeated attack traffic from a single IP address against instances in a subnet. The team must block that IP address at the subnet level as quickly as possible. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Add a low-numbered inbound deny rule for the IP address to the subnet's network ACL
Remove the subnet's route to the internet gateway until the attack stops
Create an IAM policy that denies the IP address using the aws:SourceIp condition key for all users
Add an inbound deny rule for the IP address to the instances' security group
questions.explanation: Network ACLs support explicit deny rules evaluated in number order; security groups support only allow rules.

questions.prompt: A web server's security group allows inbound HTTPS from 0.0.0.0/0, and all of its outbound rules, including the default allow-all rule, have been removed. Clients still receive responses. Why does this work?
choices: Network ACLs automatically allow all return traffic on behalf of the security groups
Security groups evaluate outbound rules only for traffic initiated by AWS services
HTTPS responses are sent through the internet gateway, which bypasses security groups
Security groups are stateful, so return traffic for allowed inbound requests is permitted
questions.explanation: Security groups track connection state, so return traffic for an allowed inbound request is allowed regardless of outbound rules.

questions.prompt: A team replaced the default network ACL on a public subnet with a custom NACL that allows inbound TCP 443 and outbound TCP 443 only. Users can no longer load the website hosted in the subnet. What is the MOST likely fix?
choices: Add an outbound rule allowing TCP ephemeral ports 1024-65535 to the client addresses
Add an outbound rule allowing all ICMP traffic to 0.0.0.0/0
Associate a second security group with the instances that allows ephemeral ports
Add an inbound rule allowing TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0
questions.explanation: NACLs are stateless, so responses to clients leave on ephemeral ports and must be explicitly allowed outbound.

questions.prompt: A three-tier application has web servers in one security group and application servers in another. The application servers must accept traffic on port 8080 only from the web servers, even as web servers scale in and out. What is the BEST way to configure this?
choices: Add an inbound rule to the application security group that allows port 8080 from the public subnet CIDR range
Add an outbound rule to the web security group that allows port 8080 to 0.0.0.0/0
Add an inbound rule to the application security group that allows port 8080 with the web tier security group as the source
Use a network ACL on the application subnet that allows port 8080 from each web server IP address
questions.explanation: Referencing a security group as the source automatically covers any instance in that group, with no IP maintenance as instances scale.

questions.prompt: An e-commerce site behind an Application Load Balancer is targeted by SQL injection and cross-site scripting attempts. Which service should a solutions architect use to block these requests?
choices: Network ACL rules on the subnets that host the load balancer
AWS WAF with a web ACL associated with the Application Load Balancer
Amazon GuardDuty findings with automated remediation through AWS Lambda
AWS Shield Standard enabled on the Application Load Balancer
questions.explanation: AWS WAF inspects HTTP requests at layer 7 and has rules for SQL injection and XSS; Shield focuses on DDoS and NACLs cannot inspect payloads.

questions.prompt: A public API behind Amazon CloudFront is being overwhelmed by a small number of clients that send thousands of requests per minute. The company wants to automatically block any IP address that exceeds a threshold. What should be used?
choices: Amazon CloudFront origin failover to a secondary origin
An AWS WAF rate-based rule in the web ACL associated with the CloudFront distribution
An AWS WAF geographic match rule that blocks the countries of the clients
A security group on the CloudFront distribution that limits connections per IP
questions.explanation: Rate-based rules count requests per IP over a time window and block addresses that exceed the limit.

questions.prompt: A financial company needs enhanced protection against large DDoS attacks for its CloudFront distributions and Elastic IPs, access to the AWS Shield Response Team, and protection against scaling charges caused by attacks. Which service meets these requirements?
choices: AWS WAF with managed rule groups
AWS Shield Advanced
AWS Firewall Manager with security group policies
AWS Shield Standard
questions.explanation: Shield Advanced adds 24/7 SRT access, advanced detection, and cost protection for attack-related scaling; Shield Standard is free but lacks those features.

questions.prompt: A media company must block viewers from specific countries from accessing its application behind an Application Load Balancer, while logging the blocked requests. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
choices: Maintain a list of country IP ranges in the ALB security group
Add an AWS WAF geo match rule to a web ACL on the ALB and enable WAF logging
Use Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing to send those countries to a nonexistent record
Write a Lambda function that checks each client IP against a geolocation database
questions.explanation: AWS WAF geo match rules use AWS-maintained IP-to-country mappings and can log blocked requests, so no IP list maintenance is required.

questions.prompt: Developers have hardcoded database credentials in an application's source code. The security team wants credentials stored centrally, retrieved at runtime, and rotated automatically without application changes for each rotation. Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: Store the credentials as plaintext parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and rotate them manually
Store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation and retrieve them at runtime
Store the credentials in an S3 bucket with default encryption and a cron job that changes them
Encrypt the credentials with AWS KMS and keep the ciphertext in the source code repository with the key ID
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager provides managed, scheduled rotation and runtime retrieval; Parameter Store does not offer native automatic rotation.

questions.prompt: An application needs to store several dozen non-secret configuration values and a few encrypted API tokens that never need automatic rotation. The company wants the LOWEST cost managed option. What should be used?
choices: AWS Secrets Manager secrets for every value, with rotation disabled to lower cost
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store standard parameters, using SecureString for the tokens
AWS AppConfig hosted configurations with each token stored as a separate Secrets Manager secret
Amazon DynamoDB with client-side encryption for the tokens
questions.explanation: Parameter Store standard parameters have no additional charge and SecureString encrypts values with KMS; Secrets Manager charges per secret and is aimed at rotation.

questions.prompt: A company's policy requires that every new Amazon EBS volume created in an account is encrypted, even when users forget to select encryption. What is the simplest way to enforce this?
choices: Enable EBS encryption by default in each Region of the account
Require users to launch instances only from encrypted AMIs
Create an AWS Config rule that deletes unencrypted volumes
Attach an SCP that denies ec2:CreateSnapshot for unencrypted volumes
questions.explanation: EBS encryption by default is a Regional account setting that automatically encrypts all new volumes and snapshot copies.

questions.prompt: A company has an existing unencrypted Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Compliance now requires encryption at rest. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Create an encrypted read replica of the unencrypted instance and promote it
Modify the DB instance and enable encryption at rest during the next maintenance window
Enable EBS encryption by default in the Region so that the existing RDS storage volumes become encrypted
Snapshot the instance, copy the snapshot with encryption, and restore from the encrypted copy
questions.explanation: Encryption cannot be enabled on an existing unencrypted RDS instance; you restore from an encrypted snapshot copy. Unencrypted instances cannot have encrypted read replicas.

questions.prompt: An EC2 instance has an unencrypted EBS data volume that must be encrypted with a customer managed KMS key. What is the correct process?
choices: Snapshot the volume, copy the snapshot with the KMS key, and create a new volume from the copy
Enable EBS encryption by default, which encrypts existing volumes at the next reboot
Stop the instance, then enable encryption on the existing volume from the EC2 console
Modify the volume type to gp3 and select encryption with the KMS key
questions.explanation: Existing volumes cannot be encrypted in place; the snapshot copy with encryption is the supported path. Encryption by default affects only new volumes.

questions.prompt: A company stores regulated data in Amazon S3. Auditors require the ability to see who used the encryption key for each object, and the company wants to control key policies and rotation. Which encryption option should be used?
choices: Server-side encryption with AWS KMS customer managed keys (SSE-KMS)
Server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3)
Server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)
Client-side encryption with keys stored on the application servers
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key gives control over the key policy and rotation, and every key use is logged in CloudTrail. SSE-S3 keys are not visible or auditable per use.

questions.prompt: A company wants to use Amazon S3 server-side encryption, but policy states that the company must supply the encryption key with every request and AWS must never store the key. Which option meets this requirement?
choices: Server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3)
Dual-layer server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (DSSE-KMS)
Server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS)
Server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)
questions.explanation: With SSE-C, S3 uses the key supplied in each request to encrypt or decrypt and then discards it, storing only a salted hash. Note that S3 now blocks SSE-C by default on new buckets, so it must be explicitly allowed in the bucket's encryption settings.

questions.prompt: A company must store cryptographic keys in dedicated, single-tenant hardware security modules that the company exclusively controls, with AWS having no access to the key material. Which service meets this requirement?
choices: AWS Secrets Manager
AWS CloudHSM
AWS Certificate Manager
AWS Key Management Service with AWS managed keys
questions.explanation: CloudHSM provides dedicated HSMs in your VPC where only you manage users and keys; KMS is a multi-tenant managed service.

questions.prompt: Account A owns a customer managed KMS key. An application in Account B needs to decrypt data encrypted with that key. What must be configured?
choices: Only an IAM policy in Account B that allows kms:Decrypt on the key ARN
A resource share in AWS Resource Access Manager that shares the key with Account B
A key policy in Account A allowing Account B, plus an IAM policy in Account B allowing key use
A copy of the key material exported from Account A and imported into a new key in Account B
questions.explanation: Cross-account KMS use requires both the key policy in the owning account and an identity policy in the using account to allow the action.

questions.prompt: A healthcare company must store medical records in Amazon S3 so that no one, including the root user, can delete or overwrite them for 7 years. Which solution meets this requirement?
choices: Use a bucket policy that denies s3:DeleteObject for all principals
Enable versioning and MFA Delete on the bucket
Enable S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a 7-year retention period
Enable S3 Object Lock in governance mode with a 7-year retention period
questions.explanation: Compliance mode prevents any user, including root, from deleting or shortening retention. Governance mode can be bypassed by users with special permission, and bucket policies can be changed.

questions.prompt: A company wants to protect objects with write-once-read-many retention but must allow a small group of security administrators to remove the retention in exceptional cases. Which configuration meets this requirement?
choices: S3 Glacier Vault Lock with a policy that the administrators can edit at any time
S3 Object Lock in governance mode, granting the administrators the s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission
S3 Versioning with a lifecycle rule that expires noncurrent versions
S3 Object Lock in compliance mode, granting the administrators the s3:PutObjectRetention permission
questions.explanation: Governance mode protects objects from most users while allowing specially permitted principals to bypass retention; compliance mode cannot be bypassed.

questions.prompt: A company's versioned S3 bucket holds critical data. The company wants to require multi-factor authentication before anyone can permanently delete an object version or change the bucket's versioning state. What should be enabled?
choices: An S3 Lifecycle rule that blocks version deletion
MFA for all IAM users in the account
MFA Delete on the bucket
S3 Object Lock in governance mode
questions.explanation: MFA Delete requires the bucket owner's MFA code to permanently delete versions or suspend versioning.

questions.prompt: A company wants to make sure that no S3 bucket in any of its accounts can ever be made public through ACLs or bucket policies, regardless of individual bucket settings. Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST effort?
choices: Add a bucket policy to every bucket that denies s3:GetObject to anonymous users
Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level and prevent changes to it with an SCP
Use Amazon Macie to scan all buckets for public access daily
Enable default encryption on all buckets in each account
questions.explanation: Account-level Block Public Access overrides bucket settings for every bucket, and an SCP stops anyone from turning it off.

questions.prompt: A company needs to give an external auditor temporary download access to a single private object in Amazon S3 for 24 hours without creating AWS credentials for the auditor. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Generate an S3 presigned URL for the object with a 24-hour expiration
Create an IAM user for the auditor and delete it after 24 hours
Make the object public and remove the public ACL after 24 hours
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration and share the accelerated endpoint
questions.explanation: A presigned URL grants time-limited access to a specific object using the signer's permissions, without new credentials.

questions.prompt: A company serves static content from a private S3 bucket through Amazon CloudFront. Users must not be able to bypass CloudFront and access the bucket directly. What is the recommended solution?
choices: Make the bucket public and require CloudFront signed URLs for every object in the distribution
Use an S3 Access Point that allows the CloudFront edge location IP ranges
Enable S3 static website hosting and restrict the website endpoint with a security group
Configure origin access control and allow only that distribution in the bucket policy
questions.explanation: OAC signs CloudFront requests to S3, and a bucket policy scoped to the distribution blocks all direct access.

questions.prompt: A video subscription service delivers hundreds of files per viewing session through Amazon CloudFront. Only paying subscribers should access the content, and the company does not want to change every URL in its player. What should be used?
choices: CloudFront signed cookies
S3 presigned URLs for each file
AWS WAF IP set rules for subscriber addresses
CloudFront signed URLs for each file
questions.explanation: Signed cookies grant access to multiple restricted files without modifying URLs; signed URLs are better for individual files.

questions.prompt: A mobile app needs user sign-up and sign-in, and signed-in users must upload photos directly to Amazon S3 using temporary AWS credentials. Which combination of services meets these requirements?
choices: An Amazon Cognito user pool alone, with the user pool tokens sent directly to S3
A Cognito user pool for sign-in and a Cognito identity pool for temporary AWS credentials
AWS IAM Identity Center for sign-in and S3 presigned URLs generated in the mobile app with root keys
An Amazon Cognito identity pool for sign-in and a separate IAM user with access keys for each app user
questions.explanation: User pools handle sign-up and sign-in; identity pools exchange those tokens for temporary IAM credentials that S3 accepts.

questions.prompt: A consumer web application must let users sign in with Google, Facebook, or Apple accounts, as well as with email and password, and must provide JWTs to the backend. Which service should be used?
choices: AWS IAM Identity Center with each social provider configured as an external identity provider
An Amazon Cognito user pool with social identity providers configured
AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory
IAM SAML 2.0 identity providers in the AWS account
questions.explanation: Cognito user pools are designed for customer identity, supporting social and native sign-in and issuing JWTs. IAM Identity Center is for workforce access.

questions.prompt: A company with 40 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations wants employees to sign in once using the company's existing Okta identity provider and receive role-based access to multiple accounts. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
choices: Use IAM Identity Center with Okta as the external identity provider and assign permission sets
Deploy an Amazon Cognito user pool federated with Okta and grant users console access through the pool
Configure an IAM SAML provider and roles separately in each of the 40 accounts
Create IAM users in each account and synchronize passwords from Okta with a script
questions.explanation: IAM Identity Center centrally manages workforce SSO to all organization accounts using permission sets, avoiding per-account configuration.

questions.prompt: A REST API built with Amazon API Gateway must allow only users who have signed in to the company's Amazon Cognito user pool. Which solution requires the LEAST custom code?
choices: Require API keys and distribute them to signed-in users
Add an API Gateway resource policy that allows the Cognito user pool ARN
Write a Lambda authorizer that validates the Cognito tokens
Configure a Cognito user pool authorizer on the API methods
questions.explanation: API Gateway natively validates Cognito user pool tokens with a Cognito authorizer, so no custom code is needed. API keys are not an authentication mechanism.

questions.prompt: A security team wants continuous detection of threats such as EC2 instances communicating with known cryptocurrency mining domains and unusual API calls from unfamiliar locations. Which service should be enabled?
choices: Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Config
Amazon Inspector
Amazon Macie
questions.explanation: GuardDuty analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs to detect threats such as crypto mining and anomalous API activity.

questions.prompt: A company has thousands of S3 buckets and must identify which objects contain personally identifiable information such as passport and credit card numbers. Which service should be used?
choices: Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Macie
AWS Audit Manager
Amazon Detective
questions.explanation: Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and classify sensitive data in Amazon S3.

questions.prompt: A company needs automated, continuous scanning of its EC2 instances, Lambda functions, and container images in Amazon ECR for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. Which service meets this requirement?
choices: Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Shield Advanced
Amazon Inspector
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector continuously scans EC2, ECR images, and Lambda for CVEs and network reachability issues.

questions.prompt: A company must continuously evaluate whether any security group allows unrestricted inbound SSH and automatically remediate noncompliant groups. Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: Use an AWS Config restricted-SSH rule with automatic remediation through SSM Automation
Enable VPC Flow Logs and review them weekly for port 22 traffic
Create a CloudWatch alarm on the NetworkIn metric for each instance
Use Amazon Inspector to scan the security groups weekly and email the findings to administrators
questions.explanation: AWS Config evaluates resource configurations against rules continuously and can trigger SSM Automation remediation.

questions.prompt: A company with many accounts in AWS Organizations must record all API activity in every account and Region into a central S3 bucket that member account administrators cannot modify. Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: Enable VPC Flow Logs in every VPC and send them to a central CloudWatch Logs group
Create an organization trail that delivers logs to a bucket in a dedicated log archive account
Use AWS Config aggregators in the management account to collect API activity from every member account
Enable CloudTrail separately in each account and let each account store logs locally
questions.explanation: An organization trail captures events for all member accounts and cannot be altered by member accounts; a separate log archive account isolates the logs.

questions.prompt: Auditors require proof that CloudTrail log files stored in Amazon S3 have not been modified or deleted after delivery. What should a solutions architect enable?
choices: CloudTrail Insights events
CloudTrail log file integrity validation
S3 default encryption with SSE-S3
S3 Transfer Acceleration on the log bucket
questions.explanation: Log file integrity validation creates signed digest files that let you verify whether log files were changed or deleted.

questions.prompt: A company uses GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and AWS Config across many accounts. The security team wants a single place to aggregate findings and check accounts against the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard. Which service should be used?
choices: AWS Security Hub
AWS Trusted Advisor
Amazon CloudWatch dashboards
Amazon Detective
questions.explanation: Security Hub aggregates findings from AWS security services and runs automated checks against standards such as FSBP and CIS.

questions.prompt: After a GuardDuty finding, a security analyst needs to quickly visualize related activity across CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and GuardDuty to determine the root cause of the incident. Which service is designed for this?
choices: Amazon Macie
AWS Config
Amazon Detective
AWS Firewall Manager
questions.explanation: Detective builds a behavior graph from log sources to help investigate and determine the root cause of findings.

questions.prompt: A company wants administrators to access shell sessions on private EC2 instances without opening inbound SSH ports, managing bastion hosts, or distributing SSH keys, and all sessions must be logged. What should be used?
choices: EC2 Instance Connect with port 22 opened to 0.0.0.0/0
A Site-to-Site VPN with SSH keys stored in Parameter Store
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager with session logging to S3 or CloudWatch Logs
A bastion host in a public subnet with SSH restricted to the corporate IP range
questions.explanation: Session Manager uses the SSM agent over outbound HTTPS, requires no inbound ports or keys, and can log full session activity.

questions.prompt: A company runs a web application behind an Application Load Balancer and must encrypt traffic between clients and the load balancer using a free, automatically renewed certificate. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Request a public ACM certificate and attach it to an HTTPS listener on the ALB
Generate a self-signed certificate on each EC2 instance and enable TCP passthrough
Import a purchased certificate into IAM and attach it to the ALB target group for HTTPS
Enable AWS Shield Standard, which encrypts traffic to the ALB automatically
questions.explanation: ACM public certificates are free for use with integrated services like ALB and renew automatically.

questions.prompt: A security policy requires that all requests to an S3 bucket use encrypted connections. Which bucket policy statement enforces this?
choices: Deny all S3 actions when the aws:SecureTransport condition key is false
Deny s3:PutObject when the aws:SourceVpce condition key is missing
Allow all S3 actions when the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption key is present
Allow only requests that include the aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent key
questions.explanation: aws:SecureTransport is false for plain HTTP requests, so denying on that condition forces HTTPS (TLS).

questions.prompt: A company must ensure that every object uploaded to a bucket is encrypted with a specific customer managed KMS key and that uploads using any other key are rejected. Which solution meets this requirement?
choices: Enable S3 Object Lock and specify the KMS key ARN in the default retention configuration of the bucket
Create an S3 Lifecycle rule that re-encrypts objects with the KMS key after upload
Set SSE-KMS default encryption with the key and deny PutObject requests that specify a different KMS key ID
Enable SSE-S3 default encryption and require clients to send the KMS key ID as object metadata
questions.explanation: Default encryption covers requests that omit headers, and the bucket policy rejects requests that specify a different KMS key.

questions.prompt: A company is deploying an Amazon CloudFront distribution with a custom domain name and wants to use a certificate from AWS Certificate Manager. In which Region must the certificate be requested or imported?
choices: Any Region, because ACM certificates are global
The Region closest to most viewers
US East (N. Virginia) us-east-1
The Region where the origin is located
questions.explanation: CloudFront only uses ACM certificates from us-east-1, regardless of where the origin is.

questions.prompt: A company needs to issue TLS certificates for hundreds of internal microservices that are not reachable from the internet, and wants a managed certificate authority hierarchy. Which service should be used?
choices: AWS CloudHSM with a self-managed CA
AWS Private Certificate Authority
ACM public certificates validated by DNS
AWS Secrets Manager with generated certificates
questions.explanation: AWS Private CA provides a managed private CA hierarchy to issue certificates for internal resources.

questions.prompt: An S3 bucket must trigger a Lambda function when new objects are created. Which permission configuration allows Amazon S3 to invoke the function?
choices: The Lambda execution role with s3:GetObject permission on the bucket
An IAM role attached to the S3 bucket that allows the lambda:InvokeFunction action on the function
A bucket policy that grants the Lambda function s3:PutBucketNotification
A resource-based policy on the function that allows the S3 service principal for that bucket
questions.explanation: Services invoke Lambda through the function's resource-based policy; the execution role only governs what the function itself can do.

questions.prompt: An IAM user has an identity-based policy that allows s3:* on a bucket. The bucket policy explicitly denies s3:DeleteObject for that user. What is the result when the user tries to delete an object?
choices: The request is denied only if the user has no permissions boundary
The request is allowed because identity-based policies take precedence over resource policies
The request is denied because an explicit deny always overrides any allow
The request is allowed because s3:* includes s3:DeleteObject
questions.explanation: In IAM policy evaluation, an explicit deny in any applicable policy overrides all allows.

questions.prompt: A company granted broad permissions to a set of roles during development. Before going to production, the company wants to generate least-privilege policies based on the actions the roles actually used. Which tool should be used?
choices: AWS Config conformance packs
AWS Trusted Advisor security checks for IAM usage
IAM Access Analyzer policy generation based on CloudTrail activity
Amazon Inspector network reachability findings for each role
questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer can review CloudTrail logs and generate a policy containing only the actions that were used.

questions.prompt: A security team must identify any S3 buckets, KMS keys, or IAM roles in the organization that are accessible to principals outside the organization. Which service provides this with the LEAST effort?
choices: IAM Access Analyzer with the organization as the zone of trust
AWS CloudTrail Lake queries across all member accounts
Amazon GuardDuty S3 Protection with organization-wide findings
Amazon Macie automated discovery
questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer analyzes resource policies and reports resources shared with external principals outside the zone of trust.

questions.prompt: A new AWS account has been created. Which action follows AWS best practices for securing the root user?
choices: Share the root user password with all administrators so that someone can always sign in
Create root access keys and store them in Secrets Manager for automation
Use the root user for daily administration tasks and an IAM user only for billing access
Enable root MFA, create no root access keys, and use other identities for daily work
questions.explanation: The root user should be protected with MFA, have no access keys, and be used only for the few tasks that require it.

questions.prompt: A security team wants to remove permissions to AWS services that IAM roles have not used in the last 90 days. Which IAM feature shows when each service was last accessed?
choices: The IAM credential report for the account
The IAM policy simulator for each role
Last accessed information (access advisor) in IAM
AWS Config resource timeline
questions.explanation: Last accessed information shows when services were last used by a principal, helping identify unused permissions to remove.

questions.prompt: A company wants developers to access only EC2 instances tagged with the same Project value as the tag on their own IAM role, without updating policies when new projects are added. Which approach should be used?
choices: ABAC with a condition matching aws:ResourceTag/Project to aws:PrincipalTag/Project
Security groups that allow or deny API access based on the instance Project tag
A separate IAM policy per project listing each instance ARN
A service control policy per project attached to separate OUs
questions.explanation: ABAC compares principal tags to resource tags, so permissions scale automatically as new projects and resources are tagged.

questions.prompt: A third-party monitoring vendor needs read access to resources in a company's AWS account. The company wants to prevent the confused deputy problem. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Create a role that trusts the vendor's account and requires a unique external ID
Create an IAM user for the vendor and send the access keys over an encrypted channel
Share the account's root credentials with the vendor using MFA
Make the resources public and restrict them with the vendor's IP addresses
questions.explanation: An external ID in the trust policy ensures the vendor assumes the role only on behalf of this customer, mitigating the confused deputy problem.

questions.prompt: A mobile app uses an Amazon Cognito identity pool to give users temporary credentials. Each user must be able to read and write only objects under their own prefix in an S3 bucket. How should the IAM policy be written?
choices: Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to move objects into per-user prefixes
Use the ${cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub} variable in the role's resource ARN
Create one bucket per user and grant the authenticated role access to all of the user buckets
Create a separate IAM role for every user and map users to roles by name
questions.explanation: The identity ID policy variable scopes a single authenticated role to each user's own prefix.

questions.prompt: A company wants applications on EC2 to connect to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL without storing database passwords, using short-lived tokens based on IAM permissions. What should be enabled?
choices: Secrets Manager rotation every hour
Kerberos authentication with AWS Managed Microsoft AD
IAM database authentication on the RDS DB instance
RDS Proxy with password authentication
questions.explanation: IAM database authentication lets applications generate a 15-minute token with their IAM role instead of using a password.

questions.prompt: A compliance rule requires that all client connections to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database be encrypted in transit. How can the database reject unencrypted connections?
choices: Enable encryption at rest with a customer managed KMS key
Set the rds.force_ssl parameter to 1 in the DB parameter group
Place the DB instance in a private subnet with no internet gateway
Enable Multi-AZ so that replication traffic is encrypted
questions.explanation: rds.force_ssl forces SSL/TLS for client connections; encryption at rest does not protect data in transit.

questions.prompt: A company stores customer data in Amazon DynamoDB and must control the encryption key, including its key policy and the ability to disable it. What should a solutions architect configure?
choices: Enable DynamoDB encryption at rest, which is off by default
Enable DynamoDB Streams with encryption enabled on the stream records
Use client-side encryption with keys stored in DynamoDB itself
Encryption at rest with a customer managed KMS key for the table
questions.explanation: DynamoDB always encrypts at rest; choosing a customer managed KMS key gives the company control over the key policy and lifecycle.

questions.prompt: A company created an Amazon EFS file system without encryption at rest. Compliance now requires encryption at rest. What must the company do?
choices: Mount the file system with the TLS option to encrypt it at rest
Apply a KMS key policy to the existing file system so new writes are encrypted
Create a new EFS file system with encryption at rest enabled and migrate the data to it
Enable encryption at rest on the existing file system from the console
questions.explanation: EFS encryption at rest can only be enabled when the file system is created; TLS in the mount helper encrypts data in transit only.

questions.prompt: A security team needs to capture metadata about IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in a VPC, including accepted and rejected connections, for troubleshooting and forensics. What should be enabled?
choices: Elastic Load Balancing access logs
AWS CloudTrail data events
VPC Flow Logs
Amazon Route 53 query logging
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs record IP traffic metadata for ENIs, subnets, or VPCs, including ACCEPT and REJECT actions.

questions.prompt: A company must inspect and filter outbound traffic from all VPCs, allowing only connections to an approved list of domain names, using a managed stateful firewall. Which service meets this requirement?
choices: Network ACLs with outbound rules for the approved domains
AWS Network Firewall with stateful domain list rules
AWS WAF web ACLs attached to the NAT gateways
Security groups with outbound rules referencing domain names
questions.explanation: Network Firewall supports stateful domain filtering for egress traffic; security groups and NACLs work only with IP addresses.

questions.prompt: A company wants to prevent workloads in its VPCs from resolving known malicious domains, with minimal changes to applications. Which feature should be used?
choices: Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones
Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall
AWS Shield Advanced
VPC DHCP option sets pointing to a public DNS server
questions.explanation: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall filters DNS queries made through the VPC resolver and can block domains on managed threat lists.

questions.prompt: A company with dozens of accounts in AWS Organizations must ensure that a standard set of AWS WAF rules is applied to every Application Load Balancer, including new ones, across all accounts. Which service should be used?
choices: AWS Control Tower account factory
AWS Config aggregators
AWS Firewall Manager
AWS Security Hub
questions.explanation: Firewall Manager centrally deploys and enforces WAF, Shield Advanced, and security group policies across accounts and new resources.

questions.prompt: A company has an AWS Direct Connect connection to its data center. A new regulation requires that all traffic between the data center and AWS be encrypted. Which solution meets this requirement while continuing to use Direct Connect?
choices: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the Direct Connect connection
Replace the private virtual interface with a hosted connection from a partner
Enable AWS Shield Advanced on the Direct Connect gateway
Enable encryption at rest on all EBS volumes and S3 buckets in the account
questions.explanation: Direct Connect is private but not encrypted by default; an IPsec VPN over it (or MACsec on supported links) adds encryption.

questions.prompt: A company is starting a multi-account strategy and wants to quickly set up a well-architected landing zone with preconfigured guardrails, a log archive account, and an audit account. Which service should be used?
choices: AWS Organizations alone
AWS CloudFormation StackSets alone
AWS Service Catalog
AWS Control Tower
questions.explanation: Control Tower automates landing zone setup with shared accounts and preventive and detective controls built on Organizations.

questions.prompt: A company wants to restrict what the root user can do in each member account of its organization. Which mechanism can restrict the root user of a member account?
choices: A resource-based policy in the management account that names the root users
A permissions boundary attached to the root user
A service control policy attached to the account or its OU
An IAM policy attached to the root user
questions.explanation: IAM policies cannot be attached to the root user, but SCPs apply to all principals in member accounts, including root.

questions.prompt: An application uses AWS Secrets Manager in us-east-1. For disaster recovery, the same secrets must be available in us-west-2 and stay in sync automatically. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Create a Lambda function that copies the secrets nightly
Store the secrets in a DynamoDB global table
Configure Secrets Manager to replicate the secrets to us-west-2
Export the secrets to an S3 bucket with Cross-Region Replication
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager multi-Region replication keeps replica secrets synchronized with the primary, including rotations.

questions.prompt: A company uses a customer managed KMS key with AWS-generated key material and must rotate the key material regularly without re-encrypting existing data. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Enable automatic key rotation on the customer managed key
Delete the key and create a new one with the same alias
Create a new key every year and re-encrypt all data with it
Switch to an AWS owned key, which never needs rotation
questions.explanation: Automatic rotation generates new key material while retaining old material so previously encrypted data can still be decrypted.

questions.prompt: A company wants to use AWS KMS keys with integrated AWS services, but compliance requires that the key material be generated and stored in single-tenant HSMs that the company controls. Which solution meets this requirement?
choices: Create AWS managed keys and enable automatic rotation
Create customer managed keys with key material generated by KMS
Create the KMS keys in an AWS CloudHSM key store
Store the keys in AWS Secrets Manager and reference them from KMS
questions.explanation: A CloudHSM key store is a KMS custom key store backed by a CloudHSM cluster you own, so key material never leaves your HSMs while services still use KMS APIs.

questions.prompt: An application encrypts data in us-east-1 and must decrypt the same ciphertext in eu-west-1 during a failover without making cross-Region KMS calls. Which KMS feature should be used?
choices: Key grants
AWS managed keys
Custom key stores
Multi-Region keys
questions.explanation: Multi-Region keys share key material and key ID across Regions, so ciphertext from one Region can be decrypted in another locally.

questions.prompt: An application must encrypt files that are several gigabytes in size using AWS KMS. What is the recommended approach?
choices: Store the file in KMS and retrieve it with the Decrypt API
Use GenerateDataKey, encrypt the file locally, and store the encrypted data key with it
Split the file into 4 KB chunks and call the KMS Encrypt API once for each of the chunks
Send the entire file to the KMS Encrypt API in a single request
questions.explanation: KMS Encrypt handles at most 4 KB, so large data uses envelope encryption with a data key.

questions.prompt: A company receives files from partner AWS accounts into its S3 bucket. The company wants to own all objects automatically and stop using ACLs entirely. What should be configured?
choices: Enable S3 Versioning and Object Lock
Enable Requester Pays on the bucket
Require partners to add the bucket-owner-full-control ACL
Set S3 Object Ownership to bucket owner enforced
questions.explanation: Bucket owner enforced disables ACLs and makes the bucket owner the owner of every object, with access controlled by policies only.

questions.prompt: Dozens of teams and applications need different access permissions to a shared S3 data lake bucket, and the bucket policy is becoming too large to manage. Which feature simplifies access management?
choices: Separate bucket ACL grants for each team and application
S3 Object Lambda functions that filter objects for each team
S3 Access Points with a dedicated access point policy for each application
S3 Batch Operations jobs that copy data per team
questions.explanation: Access points provide named endpoints, each with its own policy, which breaks one large bucket policy into manageable pieces.

questions.prompt: A company wants an S3 bucket to accept requests only from principals that belong to accounts in its AWS Organization, including accounts added in the future. Which bucket policy condition should be used?
choices: aws:SourceAccount
aws:PrincipalTag
aws:PrincipalOrgID
aws:SourceVpc
questions.explanation: aws:PrincipalOrgID matches any principal in the organization, so new accounts are covered automatically.

questions.prompt: A security review found that a web application on EC2 is vulnerable to server-side request forgery that could expose instance role credentials from the metadata service. What should a solutions architect do to reduce this risk?
choices: Move the instances into a public subnet with a stricter security group
Disable the instance profile and store keys in environment variables
Require IMDSv2 on the instances so that metadata requests need a session token
Enable EBS encryption on the root volumes
questions.explanation: IMDSv2 requires a session token obtained with a PUT request, which blocks most SSRF attempts against instance metadata.

questions.prompt: Servers running in a company's on-premises data center need to call AWS APIs. The company wants to avoid long-term access keys and already has a private certificate authority. Which solution should be used?
choices: IAM users with access keys rotated every 30 days
Amazon Cognito identity pools with unauthenticated access
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to distribute root credentials
IAM Roles Anywhere using X.509 certificates issued by the company's CA
questions.explanation: IAM Roles Anywhere lets workloads outside AWS exchange X.509 certificates for temporary IAM role credentials.

questions.prompt: Several Amazon ECS tasks with different responsibilities run on the same EC2 container instances. Each task must have only the AWS permissions it needs. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Use the ECS task execution role to grant application permissions
Assign a separate IAM task role to each task definition
Store access keys for each task in the container image
Attach a single instance role with the combined permissions of all tasks
questions.explanation: Task roles give each task its own credentials; the task execution role is for ECS agent actions like pulling images and writing logs.

questions.prompt: Pods in an Amazon EKS cluster must access different AWS services with least privilege, without sharing the worker node's IAM role. What should be used?
choices: EKS Pod Identity or IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA)
A single node instance role with permissions for all pods
Kubernetes secrets containing IAM user access keys
Security groups for pods with IAM policies attached
questions.explanation: EKS Pod Identity and IRSA associate IAM roles with Kubernetes service accounts so each pod gets its own scoped credentials.

questions.prompt: A company's internal API must be reachable only from within its VPC, and not from the internet. Which Amazon API Gateway configuration meets this requirement?
choices: A private REST API reached through an interface VPC endpoint with a resource policy
An HTTP API with API keys required on every route
An edge-optimized API with an AWS WAF rule that blocks public IP addresses
A Regional API with a security group attached that allows only the VPC CIDR
questions.explanation: Private APIs are reachable only through execute-api interface endpoints, and resource policies restrict which endpoints or VPCs can call them.

questions.prompt: A company exposes an API to partners and must identify each partner and enforce request quotas and throttling per partner. Authentication is handled separately. Which API Gateway feature meets this requirement?
choices: Stage variables configured per partner
Resource policies listing each partner's IP address
Usage plans with API keys assigned to each partner
Lambda authorizers that count requests per partner
questions.explanation: Usage plans associate API keys with throttling and quota limits; API keys identify callers but should not be the sole authentication.

questions.prompt: An API in Amazon API Gateway must validate bearer tokens issued by a third-party OAuth provider using custom logic before allowing requests. Which solution should be used?
choices: A Lambda authorizer that validates the token and returns an IAM policy
An API Gateway resource policy that checks the token value
A Cognito user pool authorizer configured with the third-party issuer
IAM authorization with Signature Version 4
questions.explanation: Lambda authorizers run custom code to validate tokens from any identity provider and return an allow or deny policy.

questions.prompt: A company wants to require user authentication for an internal web application behind an Application Load Balancer, using the corporate OpenID Connect identity provider, without changing the application code. What should be done?
choices: Place the ALB in a private subnet and require VPN access
Use Amazon CloudFront signed cookies issued by the identity provider
Configure an authenticate-oidc action on the ALB HTTPS listener rule
Add an AWS WAF rule that checks for an OIDC token header
questions.explanation: ALB can authenticate users through OIDC-compliant IdPs or Cognito before forwarding requests, offloading authentication from the app.

questions.prompt: A web form collects credit card numbers through Amazon CloudFront. The company wants those specific fields encrypted at the edge so that only a particular backend service holding the private key can decrypt them. Which feature should be used?
choices: HTTPS between CloudFront and the origin
AWS WAF managed rule groups
CloudFront field-level encryption
CloudFront origin access control
questions.explanation: Field-level encryption encrypts specified POST fields with a public key at the edge so they stay protected throughout the application stack.

questions.prompt: A company uses Amazon CloudFront with an Application Load Balancer origin. The company wants to ensure that users cannot bypass CloudFront and AWS WAF by sending requests directly to the ALB. Which solution meets this requirement?
choices: Allow only the CloudFront managed prefix list on the ALB security group and check a secret custom header
Configure CloudFront origin access control for the ALB origin and update the target groups
Enable ALB access logging and manually block unknown client IP addresses each week
Enable AWS Shield Standard on the ALB
questions.explanation: The CloudFront managed prefix list limits sources to CloudFront, and a secret header confirms the request came from your distribution. OAC applies to S3 and similar origins, not ALBs. (CloudFront VPC origins, which let the ALB live in a private subnet, are another valid option.)

questions.prompt: An Amazon RDS database must be reachable only by application servers in the same VPC. Which configuration meets this requirement?
choices: Place the DB instance in a public subnet and restrict access with a strong master password
Enable Multi-AZ and IAM database authentication while keeping a public endpoint for administrators
Allow the database port from 0.0.0.0/0 and rely on encryption in transit
Use private subnets, disable public access, and allow the DB port only from the app security group
questions.explanation: Private subnets, no public accessibility, and security group referencing limit the database to the application tier.

questions.prompt: Auditors need a record of every GetObject and PutObject request made against a specific S3 bucket that contains sensitive data. What should be configured?
choices: CloudTrail data events for the S3 bucket
VPC Flow Logs on the S3 gateway endpoint
CloudTrail management events, which are logged by default
AWS Config recording for the bucket
questions.explanation: Object-level API calls are data events, which are not logged by default and must be enabled in a trail or event data store.

questions.prompt: A company must retain its CloudTrail logs for 7 years in a way that prevents deletion by anyone, including administrators of the log archive account. Which solution meets this requirement?
choices: Enable versioning on the log bucket and deny DeleteBucket in the bucket policy
Use an S3 bucket with Object Lock in compliance mode and 7-year retention
Store the logs in an EBS volume with snapshots retained for 7 years
Deliver the logs to CloudWatch Logs with a 7-year retention setting
questions.explanation: Object Lock compliance mode makes log objects immutable for the retention period, even for administrators and root.

questions.prompt: A company wants to automatically isolate an EC2 instance whenever Amazon GuardDuty reports a high-severity finding for it. Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
choices: Enable Amazon Inspector to automatically terminate any instances that have critical vulnerabilities
Have an administrator review GuardDuty findings daily and stop affected instances
Configure GuardDuty to modify the subnet network ACLs directly when findings occur
Use an EventBridge rule on GuardDuty findings to invoke a Lambda function that applies an isolation security group
questions.explanation: GuardDuty findings are published to EventBridge, which can trigger automated responses such as security group isolation.

questions.prompt: An Amazon SQS queue holds sensitive order data. The company must encrypt messages at rest with a key whose usage is logged in CloudTrail and whose policy the company controls. Which configuration should be used?
choices: Client-side encryption with a key stored in the message attributes
Server-side encryption using SSE-KMS with a customer managed key
Server-side encryption using SQS-managed keys (SSE-SQS)
Enable SQS long polling with HTTPS endpoints
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key gives policy control and CloudTrail auditing of key use; SSE-SQS keys are managed by SQS.

questions.prompt: A company wants to protect its backups from deletion by compromised administrator accounts, as part of a ransomware defense. Backups must be immutable for a fixed period. Which solution meets this requirement?
choices: Use AWS Backup with an IAM policy that denies deletion to junior administrators
Use AWS Backup with AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode
Use EBS snapshots with tags that mark them as protected
Store backups in S3 Standard with versioning only
questions.explanation: Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode prevents anyone from deleting recovery points or changing the lifecycle once locked.

questions.prompt: A company wants backup copies stored in a separate AWS account so that a compromise of the production account cannot destroy them. Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST effort?
choices: Replicate the production account's IAM users into the backup account
Write a script that downloads snapshots to on-premises storage
Share the EBS snapshots publicly and copy them into the other account on a schedule
Use AWS Backup cross-account copy to a vault in a dedicated backup account
questions.explanation: AWS Backup supports copying recovery points to vaults in other accounts of the same organization, isolating them from the source account.

questions.prompt: A company is migrating applications that require Microsoft Active Directory features such as Group Policy and Kerberos to AWS, and needs a trust relationship with its on-premises AD. Which service should be used?
choices: Amazon Cognito user pools with SAML
AWS Managed Microsoft AD
Simple AD
AD Connector
questions.explanation: AWS Managed Microsoft AD is a real AD in AWS that supports trusts, Group Policy, and Kerberos. AD Connector only proxies to on-premises AD.

questions.prompt: A company wants Amazon WorkSpaces and other AWS directory-aware services to authenticate users against its existing on-premises Active Directory without caching any directory data in AWS. Which service should be used?
choices: Amazon Cognito identity pools
AWS Managed Microsoft AD
AD Connector
Simple AD
questions.explanation: AD Connector is a directory gateway that redirects authentication requests to the on-premises AD without storing directory information in the cloud.

questions.prompt: A team needs to share an encrypted EBS snapshot with another AWS account. The snapshot is encrypted with the default AWS managed key for EBS. What must the team do first?
choices: Copy it with a customer managed key, then share the copy and grant access to that key
Disable encryption on the snapshot before sharing it
Share the snapshot directly, because AWS managed keys are shared automatically with the target account
Make the snapshot public so the other account can copy it
questions.explanation: Snapshots encrypted with the AWS managed key cannot be shared; a customer managed key with a key policy allowing the other account is required.

questions.prompt: A software company wants to expose a single service running in its VPC to hundreds of customer VPCs without exposing the rest of its network or dealing with overlapping CIDR ranges. Which solution meets this requirement?
choices: Attach all customer VPCs to a shared transit gateway
Create VPC peering connections with each customer VPC
Expose the service through a public IP and restrict it with a security group
Create a PrivateLink endpoint service behind a Network Load Balancer
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink exposes only the specific service through interface endpoints and works even with overlapping CIDRs. Peering exposes routes and cannot overlap.

questions.prompt: A company connects many VPCs through AWS Transit Gateway. Development VPCs must not be able to communicate with production VPCs, but both must reach a shared services VPC. What should be configured?
choices: VPC peering between development and production with deny rules
A single transit gateway route table with network ACLs in each VPC
Security groups applied to each transit gateway VPC attachment to block cross-environment traffic
Separate transit gateway route tables for development and production with routes to shared services
questions.explanation: Transit gateway route table associations and propagations provide network segmentation between groups of VPCs.

questions.prompt: A company must send all traffic entering and leaving its VPCs through a fleet of third-party firewall appliances for deep packet inspection, with the ability to scale the appliances. Which service should be used?
choices: Gateway Load Balancer
Application Load Balancer
AWS Global Accelerator
Network Load Balancer with TLS listeners
questions.explanation: Gateway Load Balancer transparently distributes traffic to scalable fleets of virtual appliances using GENEVE encapsulation.

questions.prompt: Instances in a VPC use IPv6. They must be able to initiate outbound connections to the internet, but the internet must not be able to initiate connections to them over IPv6. What should be used?
choices: A virtual private gateway
An egress-only internet gateway
A NAT gateway
An internet gateway with a security group allowing all inbound IPv6
questions.explanation: An egress-only internet gateway provides outbound-only IPv6 access; NAT gateways are for IPv4 traffic.

questions.prompt: A solutions architect creates a new custom security group and does not add any rules. What traffic does the security group allow?
choices: No inbound and no outbound traffic
Inbound traffic from instances in the same security group and no outbound traffic
No inbound traffic and all outbound traffic
All inbound and all outbound traffic
questions.explanation: New security groups have no inbound rules and a default rule allowing all outbound traffic.

questions.prompt: A company wants employees to reach internal web applications without a VPN, with each request evaluated against identity and device posture policies. Which service meets this requirement?
choices: AWS Verified Access
Amazon WorkSpaces
AWS Site-to-Site VPN
AWS Client VPN
questions.explanation: Verified Access provides zero-trust access to applications by evaluating identity and device signals for each request without a VPN.

questions.prompt: A company's auditors request AWS's SOC 2 and PCI DSS compliance reports to support the company's own certification. Where can the company obtain these reports?
choices: AWS Security Hub
AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Audit Manager
AWS Artifact
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports and agreements. Audit Manager helps assess your own environment.

questions.prompt: A company suspects a customer managed KMS key is no longer used and wants to delete it, but must avoid losing access to data if the suspicion is wrong. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Delete the key immediately, because deleted keys can be restored for 30 days
Disable the key, watch CloudTrail for failed requests, then schedule deletion
Remove the key alias, which also deletes the key
Schedule deletion with a 0-day waiting period to test the impact
questions.explanation: Disabling is reversible and reveals dependencies; deletion requires a 7 to 30 day waiting period and is irreversible after it completes.

questions.prompt: A company replicates an S3 bucket encrypted with SSE-KMS to another Region. What must be configured for the replicated objects to be encrypted in the destination?
choices: Use SSE-C on the destination bucket so that the same source key material is reused
Enable KMS-encrypted object replication with a destination-Region key and role permissions
Nothing, because the source KMS key is automatically replicated along with each S3 object
Disable encryption on the source objects before replication
questions.explanation: S3 replication of SSE-KMS objects must be explicitly enabled with a destination key, and the replication role needs decrypt and encrypt permissions.

questions.prompt: An Amazon RDS for MySQL database's master user password is currently stored in a configuration file. The company wants RDS to manage the password in Secrets Manager and rotate it, with the least custom code. What should be done?
choices: Store the password in an encrypted S3 object and rotate it with S3 Lifecycle
Write a custom Lambda rotation function and store the password in Parameter Store
Enable IAM database authentication and delete the master user
Modify the DB instance to manage the master user password with Secrets Manager
questions.explanation: RDS integration with Secrets Manager creates and rotates the master user secret automatically without custom rotation code.

questions.prompt: The security team wants to be notified within minutes whenever the root user of any account signs in to the AWS Management Console. Which solution meets this requirement?
choices: Enable AWS Config to record IAM users and alert on any changes to their configuration
Run the IAM credential report daily and email it to the team
Use Amazon Inspector to detect root user activity
An EventBridge rule on root ConsoleLogin events from CloudTrail that publishes to SNS
questions.explanation: Root sign-ins are recorded by CloudTrail and can be matched in near real time by EventBridge rules that publish to SNS.

questions.prompt: A company wants to manage Amazon GuardDuty for all accounts in its organization from a security tooling account rather than the management account, and have new accounts enabled automatically. What should be done?
choices: Create a CloudFormation stack in the management account that sends invitations manually
Enable GuardDuty separately in every account and share findings by email
Use an SCP to enable GuardDuty in every account
Make the security account the GuardDuty delegated administrator with auto-enable
questions.explanation: Delegated administration lets a member account manage GuardDuty organization-wide and automatically enable new accounts.

questions.prompt: In AWS IAM Identity Center, a company wants to define a reusable set of permissions, such as read-only access, that can be assigned to groups across many accounts. Which construct should be used?
choices: Permission sets
Resource-based policies
Service control policies
IAM groups in each account
questions.explanation: Permission sets are templates of IAM policies that Identity Center provisions as roles in each assigned account.

questions.prompt: An Amazon ElastiCache for Redis OSS cluster stores session data. The company requires that clients authenticate to the cluster and that data be encrypted between clients and nodes. What should be enabled?
choices: Multi-AZ with automatic failover
In-transit encryption with Redis AUTH or role-based access control
A public endpoint with security group restrictions
Encryption at rest with a customer managed KMS key
questions.explanation: In-transit encryption provides TLS between clients and nodes, and AUTH or RBAC requires clients to authenticate.

questions.prompt: A multi-tenant application stores data in a DynamoDB table with the tenant ID as the partition key. Each user must be able to access only items with their own tenant ID. Which IAM condition key enables this fine-grained access control?
choices: dynamodb:Attributes
dynamodb:LeadingKeys
dynamodb:Select
aws:ResourceTag
questions.explanation: dynamodb:LeadingKeys restricts access to items whose partition key matches a value such as the user's identity.

questions.prompt: A company uses an S3 gateway VPC endpoint. To reduce data exfiltration risk, instances in the VPC must be able to access only the company's own buckets through the endpoint. What should be configured?
choices: A VPC endpoint policy that allows access only to the company's bucket ARNs
A network ACL rule that blocks other S3 IP ranges
S3 Block Public Access on every bucket in the company's accounts
A security group on the gateway endpoint that allows only the company's buckets
questions.explanation: Endpoint policies control which resources can be reached through the endpoint, blocking access to buckets owned by others.

questions.prompt: A company built a data lake on Amazon S3 and needs to grant analysts column-level and row-level access to tables queried through Amazon Athena, managed centrally. Which service should be used?
choices: Amazon Macie
AWS Glue DataBrew
S3 bucket policies with prefix conditions
AWS Lake Formation
questions.explanation: Lake Formation provides centralized fine-grained permissions, including column-, row-, and cell-level security for data lake tables.

questions.prompt: A company wants to protect its public website against common web exploits such as those in the OWASP Top 10 as quickly as possible, without writing its own rules. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Enable AWS Shield Standard on the website
Turn on Amazon GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring
Add AWS Managed Rules, such as the core rule set, to a WAF web ACL
Create custom network ACL rules that match each exploit pattern in the payload
questions.explanation: AWS Managed Rules are prebuilt, maintained rule groups for common threats that can be added to a web ACL immediately.

questions.prompt: An online retailer sees scraping and credential stuffing from automated clients on its CloudFront-hosted site. Which AWS WAF feature is designed to detect and manage this traffic?
choices: CloudFront origin access control
AWS WAF Bot Control managed rule group
AWS WAF geo match statements
AWS Shield Standard automatic mitigations
questions.explanation: Bot Control identifies and manages common and targeted bots, including scrapers and credential stuffing attempts.

questions.prompt: A company processes highly sensitive data, such as private keys and personal health data, on EC2 and needs an isolated compute environment that even users with administrator access to the parent instance cannot access. Which feature should be used?
choices: AWS Nitro Enclaves
EC2 Dedicated Hosts
Encrypted EBS volumes
EC2 placement groups
questions.explanation: Nitro Enclaves are isolated environments with no persistent storage, interactive access, or external networking, even from the parent instance.

questions.prompt: A company uses an AWS Organizations structure with OUs. It wants to automatically prevent any member account from disabling Amazon GuardDuty or deleting its detector. Which solution should be used?
choices: A GuardDuty suppression rule configured in each member account
An AWS Config rule that re-enables GuardDuty every hour
An IAM permissions boundary attached to the GuardDuty service-linked role
An SCP that denies guardduty:DeleteDetector and guardduty:UpdateDetector actions
questions.explanation: SCPs provide preventive guardrails that member accounts cannot override, protecting security services from being disabled.

questions.prompt: A company's Lambda function URL must be callable only by other AWS principals that sign requests with Signature Version 4. Which configuration should be used?
choices: Use the AWS_IAM auth type and grant lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl to callers
Set the function URL auth type to NONE and validate the caller inside the function
Place the function in a private subnet without an internet gateway
Attach a security group to the function URL that allows only AWS IP ranges
questions.explanation: With AWS_IAM auth, Lambda requires SigV4-signed requests from principals with lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl permission.

questions.prompt: A company must enforce a password policy for IAM users that requires a minimum of 14 characters, symbols, and expiration every 90 days. Where is this configured?
choices: The account password policy in IAM
An IAM permissions boundary
AWS Secrets Manager rotation settings
A service control policy in AWS Organizations
questions.explanation: The IAM account password policy controls complexity, length, and expiration requirements for IAM user passwords.

questions.prompt: A regulation requires that a company's EC2 instances run on hardware that is not shared with other AWS customers, but the company does not need visibility into sockets or cores. Which option meets this requirement at the LOWEST cost?
choices: Spot Instances in a cluster placement group
Dedicated Instances
Dedicated Hosts
Reserved Instances with default tenancy
questions.explanation: Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware without the host-level visibility and per-host billing of Dedicated Hosts.

questions.prompt: A company wants to ensure that an S3 bucket used for log delivery only receives objects written by AWS CloudTrail on behalf of its own organization trail, preventing other accounts' trails from writing to it. Which bucket policy condition helps achieve this?
choices: aws:SecureTransport set to false
aws:SourceArn matching the organization trail's ARN
aws:RequestedRegion set to us-east-1
aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent set to true
questions.explanation: Using aws:SourceArn (or aws:SourceAccount) in the bucket policy restricts the CloudTrail service principal to your specific trail, preventing confused deputy issues.

questions.prompt: A company stores database backups in an S3 bucket in the same account as production. A security review requires that the backups be readable by a recovery role but that the bucket deny all access from principals that do not use MFA when deleting objects. Which policy condition key should the bucket policy evaluate?
choices: aws:PrincipalOrgID
s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption
aws:SecureTransport
aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent
questions.explanation: aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent indicates whether the request was made with MFA-authenticated temporary credentials, so it can gate destructive actions.

questions.prompt: A company's application in a private subnet must download patches from the internet, but no inbound connections from the internet may reach the instances. Which solution meets this requirement for IPv4 traffic with the LEAST operational overhead?
choices: Attach an internet gateway and assign public IPs to the instances
Create a gateway VPC endpoint for the patch repository
Route outbound traffic through a NAT gateway in a public subnet
Attach an egress-only internet gateway to the private subnet
questions.explanation: A managed NAT gateway allows outbound IPv4 connections while blocking unsolicited inbound connections. Egress-only gateways work only for IPv6.

questions.prompt: A company runs a steady 24/7 compute workload that will last at least 3 years. The company expects to move parts of it from EC2 to AWS Fargate and possibly change Regions. Which purchasing option provides the LARGEST discount while keeping this flexibility?
choices: Compute Savings Plans
EC2 Instance Savings Plans
Spot Instances
Standard Reserved Instances
questions.explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply across instance families, Regions, operating systems, Fargate, and Lambda. EC2 Instance Savings Plans and Standard RIs are tied to a family and Region.

questions.prompt: A company will run m6i instances in us-east-1 continuously for 3 years and does not expect to change instance family or Region. It wants the deepest discount possible with a Savings Plan. Which option should be chosen?
choices: Convertible Reserved Instances with a 1-year term
Compute Savings Plan with a 1-year term and no upfront payment
A 3-year, all upfront EC2 Instance Savings Plan for m6i in us-east-1
On-Demand Capacity Reservations held for the full 3 years
questions.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans offer higher discounts than Compute Savings Plans in exchange for committing to a family and Region, and 3-year all upfront maximizes the discount.

questions.prompt: A research team runs large batch simulations that can be stopped and restarted at any time, and checkpoint progress to Amazon S3. Which EC2 purchasing option is MOST cost-effective?
choices: Spot Instances
Dedicated Hosts
On-Demand Instances
Reserved Instances with a 1-year term
questions.explanation: Spot Instances offer discounts of up to 90 percent and suit fault-tolerant, interruptible workloads that checkpoint their work.
