questions.prompt: A company is launching a new application with unknown usage patterns. It must run without interruption for a 2-month pilot, after which it may be shut down. Which purchasing option should be used?
choices: On-Demand Instances
A 1-year Compute Savings Plan
Spot Instances
3-year Reserved Instances
questions.explanation: On-Demand has no commitment and is not interrupted, which fits short-term, unpredictable workloads. Spot can be interrupted and commitments exceed the pilot length.

questions.prompt: A retailer needs to guarantee EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone for a 3-day sales event, but does not want a long-term commitment. What should be used?
choices: Regional Reserved Instances with a 1-year term
Spot Instances with a high maximum price
A Compute Savings Plan
On-Demand Capacity Reservations for the event period
questions.explanation: Capacity Reservations reserve capacity in a specific AZ for any duration without a term commitment. Savings Plans and regional RIs do not reserve capacity.

questions.prompt: A company is buying Reserved Instances but expects that it may need to change instance families during the term as its application evolves. Which RI type should it purchase?
choices: Zonal Standard Reserved Instances
Scheduled Reserved Instances
Convertible Reserved Instances
Standard Reserved Instances
questions.explanation: Convertible RIs can be exchanged for RIs with different families, OS, or tenancy, at a lower discount than Standard RIs.

questions.prompt: A company runs a mix of AWS Lambda functions and Fargate tasks with a predictable baseline of usage. Which option reduces the cost of this baseline?
choices: A Compute Savings Plan
EC2 Instance Savings Plans
Spot Instances for the Lambda functions
Standard Reserved Instances
questions.explanation: Compute Savings Plans are the only commitment-based discount that applies to Lambda and Fargate in addition to EC2.

questions.prompt: A stateless web tier runs in an Auto Scaling group. The company wants a guaranteed baseline of capacity and the lowest cost for additional capacity, accepting that extra capacity might occasionally be interrupted. What should a solutions architect configure?
choices: Dedicated Instances for the base capacity and Convertible Reserved Instances for scale-out
A mixed instances policy with an On-Demand base and diversified Spot above it
All Spot Instances of a single instance type
All On-Demand Instances with scheduled scaling
questions.explanation: A mixed instances policy keeps a reliable On-Demand base while using diversified Spot for cheaper scale-out capacity.

questions.prompt: A company uses Spot Instances for image processing. How much warning does EC2 give before it interrupts a Spot Instance?
choices: Thirty seconds, through an Amazon SNS message
Ten minutes, through the AWS Health Dashboard and email
Two minutes, through instance metadata and EventBridge
No warning is given before interruption
questions.explanation: EC2 issues a Spot interruption notice two minutes before interrupting the instance, available in metadata and as an EventBridge event.

questions.prompt: A company runs a large Spot fleet for batch processing and wants to minimize both interruptions and cost. Which allocation strategy is recommended?
choices: diversified with one instance type
lowest-price across a single pool
price-capacity-optimized
capacity-optimized-prioritized with On-Demand only
questions.explanation: price-capacity-optimized chooses pools with the most available capacity and the lowest prices, lowering interruption risk and cost.

questions.prompt: Development and test EC2 instances are used only from 8 AM to 6 PM on weekdays, but run 24/7. Which change reduces cost the MOST with little effort?
choices: Purchase 3-year Standard Reserved Instances for all of the development instances
Stop the instances outside business hours with a scheduler
Move the instances to Dedicated Hosts
Increase the instance size so that tests finish faster
questions.explanation: Stopping instances for nights and weekends removes roughly 70 percent of compute hours; commitments would pay for unused hours.

questions.prompt: A company suspects many of its EC2 instances are overprovisioned. It wants recommendations for smaller instance types based on historical CPU and memory utilization. Which service provides this?
choices: AWS Pricing Calculator
AWS Compute Optimizer
AWS Budgets
Amazon Inspector
questions.explanation: Compute Optimizer analyzes utilization metrics with machine learning and recommends right-sized EC2, EBS, Lambda, and other resources.

questions.prompt: A finance team wants to visualize monthly AWS spending trends by service and linked account over the past year and forecast next month's costs. Which tool should be used?
choices: AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Pricing Calculator
AWS Trusted Advisor
Amazon CloudWatch metrics
questions.explanation: Cost Explorer provides historical cost and usage analysis with filtering, grouping, and forecasting.

questions.prompt: A startup wants to receive an email alert when its forecasted monthly AWS spend is expected to exceed $5,000, and to automatically apply an IAM policy that stops new resource launches if actual spend exceeds the limit. Which service meets these requirements?
choices: AWS Cost Explorer with saved reports
AWS Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks
AWS Budgets with alerts and budget actions
AWS Cost and Usage Report delivered to S3
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets supports forecast-based alerts and budget actions that can apply IAM policies or SCPs when thresholds are crossed.

questions.prompt: A company tags all resources with a CostCenter tag but the tag does not appear as a filter in AWS Cost Explorer. What must be done?
choices: Activate CostCenter as a cost allocation tag in the Billing console
Re-create all resources with the tag applied at launch
Enable AWS Config to record the tag on all resources in every Region
Add the tag to the AWS Organizations management account
questions.explanation: User-defined tags must be activated as cost allocation tags before they appear in cost reports, and they apply going forward from activation.

questions.prompt: A company needs the most detailed hourly billing data, including resource IDs, to load into its own analytics and query with Amazon Athena. What should it use?
choices: AWS Cost Explorer's monthly view
AWS Cost and Usage Report (Data Exports) delivered to Amazon S3
The AWS Billing dashboard summary exported to CSV
AWS Budgets reports emailed to the team weekly
questions.explanation: The Cost and Usage Report, delivered through Data Exports, is the most granular billing dataset and integrates with Athena.

questions.prompt: A company wants to be alerted automatically when spending on a service suddenly spikes unexpectedly, without defining fixed thresholds for each service. Which feature should be used?
choices: Amazon CloudWatch billing alarms per service
AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
AWS Budgets with fixed thresholds
questions.explanation: Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to learn spending patterns and alert on unusual spikes without manual thresholds.

questions.prompt: Before migrating, a company wants to estimate the monthly cost of a proposed architecture that includes EC2, RDS, and S3. Which tool should a solutions architect use?
choices: AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Pricing Calculator
AWS Compute Optimizer
AWS Cost and Usage Report
questions.explanation: Pricing Calculator estimates costs for planned architectures; Cost Explorer and CUR analyze costs that have already been incurred.

questions.prompt: A company has 12 AWS accounts with separate bills. It wants a single bill and to benefit from volume pricing tiers and sharing of Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts across accounts. What should be done?
choices: Create a cross-account IAM role for the finance team
Purchase separate Savings Plans in each account
Use AWS Organizations with consolidated billing
Enable Cost Explorer in each account
questions.explanation: Consolidated billing aggregates usage for volume discounts and shares RI and Savings Plans benefits across member accounts by default.

questions.prompt: A company stores millions of objects in Amazon S3 with unpredictable and changing access patterns. Some objects are read often, others are not accessed for months. Which storage class minimizes cost without operational overhead or retrieval fees?
choices: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access
S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
questions.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering moves objects automatically between access tiers based on use, with no retrieval fees, for a small monitoring fee.

questions.prompt: A company stores monthly reports that are accessed a few times per year but must be available within milliseconds when requested and must survive the loss of an Availability Zone. Which storage class is MOST cost-effective?
choices: S3 Standard
S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
questions.explanation: Standard-IA offers millisecond access and multi-AZ resilience at lower storage cost than Standard; One Zone-IA does not survive an AZ loss.

questions.prompt: A company generates thumbnails from original images. The thumbnails are rarely accessed and can be regenerated if lost. Which storage class is the MOST cost-effective for the thumbnails?
choices: S3 Standard
S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access
questions.explanation: One Zone-IA costs less than Standard-IA and is appropriate for infrequently accessed, re-creatable data that does not need multi-AZ resilience.

questions.prompt: A hospital stores medical images that are accessed about once per quarter. When requested, images must be retrieved in milliseconds. Which storage class provides the LOWEST cost?
choices: S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
questions.explanation: Glacier Instant Retrieval offers millisecond access at lower storage cost than Standard-IA for data accessed about once a quarter.

questions.prompt: A company archives project files that are almost never accessed. When they are needed, a retrieval time of a few hours is acceptable, and occasionally free bulk retrievals are useful. Which storage class fits BEST at low cost while allowing retrieval within hours?
choices: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access
S3 Intelligent-Tiering Frequent Access tier
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
questions.explanation: Glacier Flexible Retrieval offers retrievals from minutes to hours, including free bulk retrievals, at lower cost than Instant Retrieval.

questions.prompt: A financial firm must keep transaction records for 10 years for regulatory reasons. The records will likely never be read, and a retrieval time of up to 48 hours is acceptable. Which storage class is the MOST cost-effective?
choices: S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access
S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access
questions.explanation: Deep Archive is the lowest-cost S3 storage class, with retrievals within 12 to 48 hours, ideal for long-term compliance archives.

questions.prompt: Log files in an S3 bucket are queried frequently for the first 30 days, occasionally for the next 60 days, and must then be kept for 1 year for audits before deletion. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
choices: Store logs on EBS gp3 volumes and take snapshots after 90 days
Keep all objects in S3 Standard and have an operator delete them manually after 1 year
Store all logs in S3 Glacier Deep Archive from the start
A lifecycle policy: Standard-IA at 30 days, Glacier Flexible Retrieval at 90, expire at 365
questions.explanation: Lifecycle transitions match storage class to access patterns, and expiration removes objects automatically after the retention period.

questions.prompt: A solutions architect creates a lifecycle rule to move new objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-IA after 7 days, but the configuration is rejected. Why?
choices: Standard-IA can only receive objects from S3 Glacier
Objects must stay in S3 Standard for at least 30 days first
Lifecycle rules can only transition objects that are at least 90 days old
Standard-IA requires S3 Versioning to be suspended
questions.explanation: S3 requires a minimum of 30 days in Standard before a lifecycle transition to Standard-IA or One Zone-IA.

questions.prompt: A versioned S3 bucket's storage costs keep growing because objects are frequently overwritten, leaving many old versions. The company needs to keep previous versions for only 30 days. What should be done?
choices: Add a lifecycle rule that expires noncurrent versions after 30 days
Enable S3 Object Lock with a 30-day retention
Suspend versioning on the bucket
Move the current versions to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days
questions.explanation: NoncurrentVersionExpiration removes old versions after a set number of days, controlling the cost of versioning.

questions.prompt: A company's S3 bill includes storage for parts of large uploads that failed and were never completed. How can these charges be eliminated automatically?
choices: Add a lifecycle rule that aborts incomplete multipart uploads
Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering on the bucket
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket
Turn on S3 Versioning so the parts are merged into objects
questions.explanation: Incomplete multipart upload parts are billed until removed; the AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle action cleans them up.

questions.prompt: A company wants data-driven guidance on when to transition objects in a bucket from S3 Standard to Standard-IA based on observed access patterns. Which feature should be used?
choices: S3 Inventory encryption reports
S3 Batch Replication
S3 Object Lambda
S3 Storage Class Analysis
questions.explanation: Storage Class Analysis observes access patterns and recommends when to move data to Standard-IA.

questions.prompt: A research institute shares a large public dataset in Amazon S3 with other organizations. The institute wants the organizations that download the data to pay for the data transfer and request costs. What should be enabled?
choices: Cross-Region Replication to the requesters' Regions
Requester Pays on the bucket
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
S3 Transfer Acceleration
questions.explanation: With Requester Pays, the requester pays request and data transfer charges while the bucket owner pays for storage.

questions.prompt: An application writes millions of small objects per day to an S3 bucket using SSE-KMS, and AWS KMS request charges have become significant. Which change reduces KMS costs with the LEAST effort?
choices: Switch to client-side encryption with a key per object
Enable S3 Bucket Keys for the bucket
Create a new KMS key for every day of data
Use SSE-C with keys stored in Secrets Manager
questions.explanation: S3 Bucket Keys generate a bucket-level key that reduces calls to KMS by up to 99 percent.

questions.prompt: EC2 instances in private subnets send large volumes of data to Amazon S3 in the same Region through a NAT gateway, producing high NAT data processing charges. Which change reduces these costs the MOST?
choices: Create an interface VPC endpoint for S3 in every Availability Zone of the VPC
Move the instances to public subnets and use Transfer Acceleration
Replace the NAT gateway with a larger NAT gateway
Add an S3 gateway VPC endpoint to the private route tables
questions.explanation: Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB have no hourly or data processing charges, unlike NAT gateways and interface endpoints.

questions.prompt: A company serves large video files directly from an S3 bucket to viewers around the world and has high data transfer out costs. Which solution reduces cost and improves performance?
choices: Replicate the bucket to every Region with Cross-Region Replication
Move the files to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for all downloads
Serve the files through CloudFront with S3 as the origin
questions.explanation: Data transfer from S3 to CloudFront is free, CloudFront's data transfer out rates are typically lower, and caching reduces origin requests.

questions.prompt: Which statement about AWS data transfer pricing is correct?
choices: Data transferred out to the internet is free for the first 1 PB each month
Data transferred between Regions is free when using private IP addresses
Data transferred between Availability Zones is always free
Data transferred into AWS from the internet is generally free
questions.explanation: Inbound data transfer is generally free; inter-AZ, inter-Region, and outbound internet transfer are typically charged.

questions.prompt: Two EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone exchange large amounts of data. How should they communicate to avoid data transfer charges?
choices: Use their private IP addresses
Route traffic through a NAT gateway in the same AZ
Use their public IPv4 addresses
Use Elastic IP addresses attached to each instance
questions.explanation: Traffic between instances in the same AZ over private IPs is free; using public or Elastic IPs incurs data transfer charges.

questions.prompt: A company needs to move 80 TB of data from its data center to Amazon S3 within two weeks. Its internet connection is 100 Mbps and is heavily used by other traffic. Which option is the MOST cost-effective and timely?
choices: Upload the data over the internet with S3 Transfer Acceleration
Use AWS DataSync over the existing internet connection
Provision a new 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection for the transfer
Order AWS Snowball Edge devices and ship the data to AWS
questions.explanation: At 100 Mbps, 80 TB would take months; Snowball Edge moves the data offline quickly without the lead time and cost of new Direct Connect.

questions.prompt: A company transfers tens of terabytes per month from AWS to its on-premises data center over the internet. The data transfer out charges are high and consistent each month. Which solution can reduce these charges?
choices: Use AWS Direct Connect, which has lower data transfer out rates
Compress the data with Amazon CloudFront before sending it to the data center
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source buckets
Use a Site-to-Site VPN over the internet to avoid data transfer charges
questions.explanation: Data transfer out over Direct Connect is billed at lower rates than internet data transfer, which pays off for large, steady volumes. VPN traffic still uses internet rates.

questions.prompt: A company uses many gp2 EBS volumes. It wants to reduce storage costs while keeping the same baseline performance, and it would like to set IOPS independently of volume size. What should it do?
choices: Migrate the volumes to io2 Block Express
Migrate the volumes to gp3 using Elastic Volumes
Replace the volumes with instance store volumes
Migrate the volumes to st1
questions.explanation: gp3 costs up to 20 percent less per GB than gp2 and provides a 3,000 IOPS baseline with IOPS and throughput provisioned independently of size.

questions.prompt: A cost review finds hundreds of EBS volumes that are not attached to any instance and old snapshots that must be kept for compliance but are rarely restored. Which actions reduce cost? (Choose the BEST option.)
choices: Convert the unattached volumes to io2 and keep all snapshots in the standard tier
Copy the snapshots to another Region with lower storage pricing and delete the originals
Attach all volumes to a single instance to avoid volume charges
Delete unneeded unattached volumes and archive the compliance snapshots
questions.explanation: Unattached volumes still incur charges, and the snapshot archive tier is up to 75 percent cheaper for rarely restored snapshots.

questions.prompt: A company needs block storage for large, sequential datasets that are accessed only a few times per month, and wants the LOWEST cost per GB for EBS. Which volume type should be used?
choices: Cold HDD (sc1)
General Purpose SSD (gp3)
Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2)
Throughput Optimized HDD (st1)
questions.explanation: sc1 has the lowest cost per GB of all EBS volume types and is designed for infrequently accessed, throughput-oriented data.

questions.prompt: A company stores files on Amazon EFS. Most files are not accessed after 30 days, but users occasionally open older files. Which change reduces cost with the LEAST effort?
choices: Switch the file system to Provisioned Throughput mode with a lower throughput setting
Move all files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive with a script
Enable EFS lifecycle management to move files to EFS IA after 30 days
Replace EFS with EBS volumes attached to each instance
questions.explanation: EFS lifecycle management automatically moves files not accessed for a set period to the lower-cost IA class while keeping them in the same file system.

questions.prompt: A development team needs a shared file system for test workloads that does not require Multi-AZ resilience. Which option provides the LOWEST cost on Amazon EFS?
choices: An Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ file system
An EFS Regional file system with Max I/O performance mode
An EFS One Zone file system
An EFS Regional file system with Provisioned Throughput
questions.explanation: EFS One Zone storage classes cost less than Regional ones by storing data in a single AZ, suitable for non-critical workloads.

questions.prompt: A company runs a production Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database with a stable size and constant load, and expects to keep it for 3 years. Which option reduces database cost the MOST?
choices: Convert the database to Aurora Serverless v2
Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan
Run the database on Spot Instances
Purchase RDS Reserved Instances for the DB instance class
questions.explanation: RDS Reserved Instances discount steady-state databases significantly; EC2 Savings Plans do not apply to RDS.

questions.prompt: An internal reporting application's database is idle most of the day and has unpredictable bursts of activity. The company wants to pay only for the capacity it uses while keeping MySQL compatibility. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
choices: Amazon RDS for MySQL on a large provisioned instance
Amazon Aurora provisioned with three read replicas
MySQL on EC2 Reserved Instances
Amazon Aurora Serverless v2
questions.explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity automatically in fine-grained increments, matching cost to intermittent and variable load.

questions.prompt: A company's Aurora cluster has very high I/O activity, and I/O charges make up more than 25 percent of its Aurora bill. Which change can reduce cost?
choices: Enable Aurora Backtrack
Move the cluster to a larger instance class
Switch the cluster to Aurora Standard storage with more replicas
Switch the cluster to the Aurora I/O-Optimized storage configuration
questions.explanation: Aurora I/O-Optimized has no per-request I/O charges, which lowers cost for I/O-intensive workloads where I/O exceeds about 25 percent of spend.

questions.prompt: A new DynamoDB-backed application has unpredictable traffic with sudden spikes and long idle periods. Which capacity mode is MOST cost-effective?
choices: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) with provisioned capacity
Provisioned capacity mode with reserved capacity
On-demand capacity mode
Provisioned capacity mode without auto scaling
questions.explanation: On-demand mode charges per request and needs no capacity planning, which suits spiky or unpredictable workloads.

questions.prompt: A DynamoDB table has steady, predictable traffic that varies slightly throughout the day. The company wants to minimize cost. What should be configured?
choices: Provisioned mode with auto scaling and reserved capacity
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of an on-demand capacity table
A global table replicated in three Regions for read distribution
On-demand capacity mode
questions.explanation: For predictable traffic, provisioned capacity with auto scaling is cheaper than on-demand, and reserved capacity further discounts the baseline.

questions.prompt: A DynamoDB table stores order history that is rarely read after the first month, and storage is now the dominant cost of the table. Which change reduces cost?
choices: Enable DynamoDB Streams on the table
Change the table class to DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access
Switch the table to on-demand capacity mode
Add a global secondary index on the order date
questions.explanation: Standard-IA table class lowers storage costs by about 60 percent for tables where storage dominates, with higher read and write prices.

questions.prompt: Session records in a DynamoDB table are useless after 24 hours. The company wants them removed automatically without consuming write capacity. What should be used?
choices: A scheduled Lambda function that scans and deletes old items
A lifecycle policy on the table
DynamoDB Streams with a filter on old items
DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL) on an expiration timestamp attribute
questions.explanation: TTL deletes expired items in the background at no extra cost and without consuming write capacity.

questions.prompt: A read-heavy application repeatedly runs the same queries against an Amazon RDS database, forcing the company to run a very large DB instance. Which solution can lower cost while improving response times?
choices: Enable Multi-AZ on the DB instance
Migrate the database to a Dedicated Host
Cache frequent query results in ElastiCache and downsize the database
Increase the Provisioned IOPS on the database storage to speed up the repeated queries
questions.explanation: Caching offloads repeated reads, allowing a smaller database instance; Multi-AZ adds cost and its standby does not serve reads.

questions.prompt: A company runs a small EC2 instance 24/7 to process files that arrive a few times per day, with each job taking about 2 minutes. Which architecture is MOST cost-effective?
choices: Purchase a 3-year Reserved Instance for the existing instance
Run the processing on an Amazon EMR cluster
Process each file with Lambda triggered by S3 events
Use a larger EC2 instance so that jobs complete faster
questions.explanation: Lambda charges only for execution time, eliminating the cost of an idle server for infrequent, short jobs.

questions.prompt: A company wants to lower the cost of its Lambda functions and EC2 fleet running Linux workloads without major code changes. Which option offers better price performance for compatible workloads?
choices: Move compatible workloads to AWS Graviton (Arm-based) processors
Move the workloads to x86 Dedicated Hosts
Run the EC2 instances with Dedicated tenancy
Increase Lambda memory to the maximum for all functions
questions.explanation: Graviton-based EC2 instances and arm64 Lambda functions offer better price performance than comparable x86 options for compatible code.

questions.prompt: A company runs interruption-tolerant containerized batch jobs on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. How can it reduce compute cost the MOST?
choices: Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans
Increase the task CPU and memory reservations
Run the tasks on Dedicated Hosts
Run the tasks with the Fargate Spot capacity provider
questions.explanation: Fargate Spot runs tasks on spare capacity at a significant discount and can be interrupted with a two-minute warning.

questions.prompt: Analysts use Amazon Athena to query CSV logs stored in S3, and query costs are high because each query scans the full dataset. Which change reduces costs the MOST?
choices: Move the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
Convert the data to partitioned, compressed Parquet files
Run the queries from a larger EC2 instance with more memory and CPU
Enable S3 Versioning on the data bucket
questions.explanation: Athena charges per data scanned; columnar formats, compression, and partitioning dramatically reduce the bytes read per query.

questions.prompt: A company's Amazon Redshift cluster is running out of storage because it holds several years of historical data that is queried only occasionally. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
choices: Move the historical data to Amazon EBS snapshots and restore them when queried
Add more nodes to the cluster to store the historical data
Migrate the entire warehouse to Amazon RDS
Unload historical data to S3 and query it with Redshift Spectrum
questions.explanation: Redshift Spectrum queries data directly in low-cost S3 storage, avoiding cluster growth for rarely queried data.

questions.prompt: A company runs Amazon EMR clusters for nightly Spark jobs. The jobs can tolerate the loss of some worker nodes. How can the company reduce cost while protecting cluster stability?
choices: Use Spot Instances for the primary node and On-Demand for task nodes
Keep the cluster running 24/7 with Reserved Instances for all nodes
On-Demand primary and core nodes with Spot task nodes
Use Dedicated Hosts for all nodes
questions.explanation: Task nodes store no HDFS data, so Spot interruptions there do not risk data loss; the primary and core nodes remain stable on On-Demand.

questions.prompt: Application logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs are kept forever by default, and storage costs keep growing. Logs are needed for only 30 days. What should be done?
choices: Switch the log groups to a different Region
Delete and re-create the log groups every month
Create a lifecycle rule on the log groups to move logs to Glacier
Set a 30-day retention policy on the log groups
questions.explanation: Log groups default to never expire; a retention policy automatically deletes older log events.

questions.prompt: A company ingests large volumes of debug logs into CloudWatch Logs that are rarely queried and do not need features such as live tail or metric filters. Which option reduces ingestion costs?
choices: Use a Standard log class with metric filters
Increase the retention period to 10 years
Use the CloudWatch Logs Infrequent Access log class for those log groups
Enable CloudWatch Logs Insights on the log groups
questions.explanation: The Infrequent Access log class has a lower ingestion price in exchange for a reduced feature set.

questions.prompt: A cost review shows charges for public IPv4 addresses, including Elastic IP addresses that are not associated with running instances. Which action reduces these charges?
choices: Convert the Elastic IP addresses to secondary private IPs
Move the Elastic IP addresses to another Region
Associate each unused Elastic IP address with a stopped instance to avoid the idle charge
Release unused Elastic IPs and stop assigning unneeded public IPv4 addresses
questions.explanation: AWS charges hourly for all public IPv4 addresses, including idle Elastic IPs; releasing them and using private or IPv6 addressing lowers cost.

questions.prompt: A company is migrating a commercial database that is licensed per physical CPU socket and wants to bring its existing licenses to AWS. Which EC2 option is MOST cost-effective while meeting licensing terms?
choices: Spot Instances
Dedicated Instances
Shared-tenancy On-Demand Instances
Dedicated Hosts
questions.explanation: Dedicated Hosts provide visibility into physical sockets and cores, which is required for many BYOL licensing models.

questions.prompt: An Auto Scaling group is sized for peak traffic at all times, but average CPU usage is 15 percent. Traffic varies throughout the day without a fixed schedule. What should a solutions architect do to reduce cost?
choices: Replace the instances with larger instances and fewer of them
Disable scaling and add instances manually when alarms fire
Add a target tracking policy on average CPU and lower the minimum capacity
Purchase Reserved Instances for the peak number of instances
questions.explanation: Target tracking adjusts capacity to demand, so the group no longer pays for peak capacity during quiet periods.

questions.prompt: A company's traffic rises sharply every weekday at 9 AM and drops at 6 PM. The company wants to avoid paying for excess capacity overnight while having capacity ready before the morning rush. What should be used?
choices: Spot Instances with no scaling policy
Scheduled scaling actions for the Auto Scaling group
Manual scaling by an operator each morning
A Compute Savings Plan sized for peak
questions.explanation: Scheduled scaling changes capacity at known times, providing capacity before the predictable peak and reducing it afterward.

questions.prompt: A company wants a quick list of idle load balancers, underutilized EC2 instances, and unassociated Elastic IP addresses across its account. Which service provides these cost optimization checks?
choices: AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Artifact
AWS Trusted Advisor
questions.explanation: Trusted Advisor includes cost optimization checks such as idle load balancers, low-utilization instances, and unassociated Elastic IPs.

questions.prompt: A company hosts a static marketing website made of HTML, CSS, and images on two EC2 instances behind a load balancer. Which architecture is MOST cost-effective?
choices: Run the website on Amazon ECS with Fargate
Move the website to larger EC2 Reserved Instances
Host the website on an Amazon RDS instance
Host the files in Amazon S3 and serve them through Amazon CloudFront
questions.explanation: S3 with CloudFront serves static content with no servers to run, costing far less than EC2 instances and a load balancer.

questions.prompt: A company is building a new API that needs simple JWT authorization and proxying to Lambda, and does not need features such as usage plans or request validation. Which API Gateway option is the MOST cost-effective?
choices: WebSocket API
REST API with private endpoints
REST API with edge-optimized endpoints
HTTP API
questions.explanation: HTTP APIs cost significantly less than REST APIs and support JWT authorizers and Lambda proxy integrations.

questions.prompt: A worker application polls an Amazon SQS queue continuously, and most ReceiveMessage calls return no messages, increasing request costs. Which change reduces cost?
choices: Switch the queue to a FIFO queue with content-based deduplication
Poll the queue from more consumers at the same time
Decrease the visibility timeout to 0 seconds
Enable long polling with a wait time of up to 20 seconds
questions.explanation: Long polling waits for messages to arrive, reducing the number of empty responses and therefore the number of billed requests.

questions.prompt: A company runs millions of short-lived, high-volume event-processing workflows per day with AWS Step Functions. Each workflow finishes in a few seconds and does not need exactly-once execution. Which option is MOST cost-effective?
choices: Step Functions Express Workflows
Step Functions Standard Workflows
Amazon EC2 instances running a custom workflow engine
Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow)
questions.explanation: Express Workflows are priced by requests and duration and suit high-volume, short workflows; Standard Workflows charge per state transition.

questions.prompt: A company needs to restore 50 TB of data from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval for a project starting in two days. Which retrieval option is the MOST cost-effective while meeting the deadline?
choices: Bulk retrieval
Copying the objects directly to S3 Standard without a restore
Expedited retrieval
Standard retrieval with provisioned capacity
questions.explanation: Bulk retrievals from Glacier Flexible Retrieval are free and typically complete within 5 to 12 hours, well within two days.

questions.prompt: A company moves objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive and deletes some of them 60 days later. What will the company be charged?
choices: A retrieval fee for each deleted object
A charge for 90 days, which is the minimum duration for all Glacier storage classes
No charge, because Deep Archive has no minimum storage duration
A prorated charge for the rest of the 180-day minimum duration
questions.explanation: Deep Archive has a 180-day minimum storage duration, so deleting objects earlier incurs a prorated charge for the remaining days.

questions.prompt: A company uses AWS Backup to keep EBS and EFS backups for 1 year. Most backups are never restored after the first month. How can backup storage costs be reduced?
choices: Store the backups in S3 Standard with versioning
Delete all backups after 7 days
Move recovery points to cold storage after 30 days in the plan lifecycle
Copy the backups to another Region every day and delete the source copies
questions.explanation: AWS Backup lifecycle rules can transition supported recovery points to lower-cost cold storage, which has a 90-day minimum retention.

questions.prompt: In a Savings Plan purchase, what does the company commit to?
choices: A specific number of instances of a fixed size and family for exactly 1 year
A fixed number of vCPUs in each Availability Zone
A monthly maximum bill that AWS cannot exceed
A dollar-per-hour amount of compute usage for 1 or 3 years
questions.explanation: Savings Plans are a commitment to a dollar-per-hour amount of usage; usage above the commitment is billed at On-Demand rates.

questions.prompt: A company no longer needs some Standard Reserved Instances it purchased with 2 years left on the term. What can it do to recover some of the cost?
choices: Transfer the Reserved Instances to a Spot Fleet
Convert the Standard Reserved Instances to a Compute Savings Plan
Sell them on the Reserved Instance Marketplace
Request a full refund through AWS Support
questions.explanation: Standard RIs can be listed on the Reserved Instance Marketplace; Convertible RIs cannot be sold there.

questions.prompt: A company wants a Reserved Instance discount and also needs a capacity reservation for its instances in a particular Availability Zone. Which type of RI should be purchased?
choices: A regional Reserved Instance
A zonal Reserved Instance
A Convertible regional Reserved Instance
A Compute Savings Plan
questions.explanation: Zonal RIs reserve capacity in a specific AZ; regional RIs provide AZ flexibility and instance size flexibility but no capacity reservation.

questions.prompt: A company uses physical tape libraries for long-term backups and wants to eliminate tape hardware costs while keeping its existing backup software. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
choices: Amazon EFS with lifecycle management that moves backup files to EFS IA
AWS Snowball Edge devices shipped each month
Storage Gateway Tape Gateway archiving to Glacier Deep Archive
Amazon EBS cold HDD volumes attached to a backup server
questions.explanation: Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library to existing backup software and can archive tapes to low-cost Glacier storage classes.

questions.prompt: A company has multiple business units in separate accounts within AWS Organizations. Finance wants to group costs into business-defined categories, such as by product line combining accounts and tags. Which feature should be used?
choices: AWS Cost Categories
Service control policies
AWS Resource Groups
AWS Config conformance packs
questions.explanation: Cost Categories map costs to custom groupings using rules based on accounts, tags, and services for reporting in Cost Explorer and Budgets.

questions.prompt: A small business needs a simple virtual server with predictable monthly pricing that bundles compute, storage, and data transfer for a WordPress site. Which service is the MOST cost-effective and simple?
choices: AWS Elastic Beanstalk with a multi-AZ RDS database
Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts
Amazon EKS
Amazon Lightsail
questions.explanation: Lightsail offers low, predictable monthly plans that bundle compute, storage, and data transfer for simple workloads.

questions.prompt: A company uses Amazon CloudFront, and most of its users are in North America and Europe. The company wants to reduce CloudFront costs and accepts slightly higher latency for users elsewhere. What should be changed?
choices: Enable Origin Shield in every Region near the users
Choose a lower price class, such as Price Class 100
Add a second origin in Asia
Disable caching for all objects
questions.explanation: Price classes limit the edge locations used to lower-priced regions, reducing cost at the expense of latency elsewhere.

questions.prompt: A development RDS database is needed only a few days per month. The team wants to avoid paying for DB instance hours when it is not in use. What should be done?
choices: Convert the database to a read replica
Purchase a Reserved Instance for the development database
Stop the instance when idle, noting it restarts after 7 days
Enable Multi-AZ so that the standby absorbs the instance charges
questions.explanation: Stopped RDS instances incur only storage charges, but RDS automatically starts them after 7 days, so they must be stopped again or automated.

questions.prompt: A company replicates all objects in a 500 TB bucket to another Region for compliance, but only the objects under the legal/ prefix must be replicated. Which change reduces cost?
choices: Replace Cross-Region Replication with Same-Region Replication
Store the destination objects in S3 Standard
Limit the replication rule with a filter for the legal/ prefix
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the destination bucket
questions.explanation: Scoping replication rules with prefix or tag filters avoids inter-Region transfer and storage costs for unnecessary objects.

questions.prompt: A data pipeline copies data between EC2 instances in different Availability Zones many times per hour, and inter-AZ data transfer costs are high. The workload is a non-critical batch job that does not need multi-AZ resilience. What is the MOST cost-effective change?
choices: Route the traffic through a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone
Run the batch instances in a single Availability Zone
Use public IP addresses for the transfers
Add a Transit Gateway between the subnets
questions.explanation: Data transfer between AZs is charged in both directions, while traffic in one AZ over private IPs is free; this is acceptable for non-critical workloads.

questions.prompt: A company is evaluating whether to purchase a Savings Plan and wants AWS to recommend a commitment amount based on its past usage. Where can it find this recommendation?
choices: Amazon CloudWatch billing alarms
AWS Pricing Calculator
Savings Plans recommendations in AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Compute Optimizer rightsizing reports for EBS volumes
questions.explanation: Cost Explorer analyzes historical usage and recommends Savings Plans commitments and their estimated savings.

questions.prompt: A company has 30 VPCs, each with its own set of identical interface VPC endpoints for services such as Amazon SQS and AWS STS. The VPCs are already connected through AWS Transit Gateway. Which change reduces endpoint costs the MOST?
choices: Centralize the interface endpoints in a shared services VPC and resolve them from the other VPCs through Route 53 private hosted zones
Create additional interface endpoints in every Availability Zone of each VPC
Replace every interface endpoint with a NAT gateway in each VPC
Convert the interface endpoints to gateway endpoints for SQS and STS
questions.explanation: Interface endpoints are billed per hour per AZ, so sharing one set from a central VPC removes duplicate charges. Gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB.

questions.prompt: A company with many accounts wants an organization-wide view of Amazon S3 usage and activity, including recommendations such as buckets without lifecycle rules for incomplete multipart uploads. Which feature should be used?
choices: AWS Cost and Usage Report filtered by bucket
S3 Storage Class Analysis on one bucket
S3 Inventory reports for the largest bucket
Amazon S3 Storage Lens
questions.explanation: S3 Storage Lens aggregates usage and activity metrics across accounts and Regions and highlights cost-optimization opportunities.

questions.prompt: A company runs a MySQL database on Amazon RDS. The business requires automatic failover with no data loss if the primary database instance's Availability Zone fails. What should a solutions architect configure?
choices: Create a read replica in another Availability Zone
Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the RDS DB instance
Place the DB instance in a larger instance class
Take automated snapshots every 5 minutes
questions.explanation: RDS Multi-AZ keeps a synchronously replicated standby in another AZ and fails over automatically. Read replicas use asynchronous replication and require manual promotion.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the standby instance in a classic RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment (one standby) is correct?
choices: It must be in a different AWS Region
It serves read traffic through a separate reader endpoint
It cannot serve read traffic; it exists only for failover
It replicates asynchronously from the primary
questions.explanation: In a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment the standby is not readable. Readable standbys are a feature of Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments, which have two readable standbys.

questions.prompt: An application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer must keep running if an entire Availability Zone fails. The instances are in an Auto Scaling group. What is the MOST important configuration?
choices: Enable termination protection on every instance in the group
Use a larger instance type in a single Availability Zone
Span the Auto Scaling group and ALB across multiple AZs
Attach an Elastic IP address to each instance in the group
questions.explanation: Spreading the Auto Scaling group and ALB across multiple AZs lets traffic and capacity shift away from a failed AZ. Bigger instances in one AZ remain a single point of failure.

questions.prompt: An order-processing web tier sends orders directly to a backend that sometimes becomes overwhelmed, causing lost orders. The company wants to decouple the tiers so that no orders are lost during spikes. Which solution is MOST appropriate?
choices: Increase the backend instance size and keep direct calls
Have the web tier write orders to an Amazon SQS queue that the backend polls
Have the web tier publish orders to an Amazon SNS topic with no subscribers
Store orders in instance store volumes on the web servers
questions.explanation: SQS durably buffers messages until consumers process them, absorbing spikes. An SNS topic without subscribers does not store messages.

questions.prompt: A workload must process each message exactly once and in the exact order it was sent for each customer. Which service configuration meets this requirement?
choices: An Amazon SNS standard topic with an SQS standard subscriber
An Amazon SQS standard queue with an attached dead-letter queue
An Amazon SQS standard queue with long polling enabled on it
An Amazon SQS FIFO queue using the customer ID as the message group ID
questions.explanation: FIFO queues provide ordering within a message group and exactly-once processing with deduplication. Standard queues provide at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering.

questions.prompt: Messages in an Amazon SQS queue occasionally fail processing repeatedly and block analysis of other messages. The team wants failed messages set aside for later investigation. What should they configure?
choices: A delay queue configured with the maximum 15-minute delay
A longer message retention period on the source queue
A shorter visibility timeout configured on the source queue
A dead-letter queue with a redrive policy and a maxReceiveCount
questions.explanation: A redrive policy moves messages to a dead-letter queue after they have been received maxReceiveCount times without being deleted, isolating poison messages.

questions.prompt: Consumers of an Amazon SQS queue take up to 4 minutes to process a message, and messages are sometimes processed twice by different consumers. What is the MOST likely fix?
choices: Decrease the message retention period on the queue to 1 hour
Convert the queue into a delay queue with a 4-minute delay
Increase the queue's visibility timeout to exceed the maximum processing time
Enable long polling by setting ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds to 20
questions.explanation: If processing exceeds the visibility timeout (30 seconds by default), the message becomes visible again and another consumer receives it. Long polling reduces empty responses but does not prevent duplicates.

questions.prompt: A company wants one event published by an order service to be delivered to three independent processing services, each of which must be able to buffer messages if it is temporarily down. Which design is BEST?
choices: Send the event to a single SQS queue polled by all three services
Publish to an Amazon SNS topic that fans out to three Amazon SQS queues
Invoke each service synchronously from the order service
Write the event to an S3 bucket and have services list the bucket
questions.explanation: SNS-to-SQS fan-out gives each subscriber its own durable queue. A single shared queue would deliver each message to only one of the services.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum message retention period that can be configured for an Amazon SQS queue?
choices: 4 days
7 days
30 days
14 days
questions.explanation: SQS retention is configurable from 60 seconds to 14 days; the default is 4 days.

questions.prompt: A company must recover its on-premises application in AWS within 24 hours of a disaster, and cost must be as low as possible. Data loss of up to one day is acceptable. Which disaster recovery strategy fits BEST?
choices: Multi-site active/active
Backup and restore
Pilot light
Warm standby
questions.explanation: Backup and restore has the lowest cost and the longest RTO/RPO, which matches a 24-hour recovery target. The other strategies cost more because they keep resources running.

questions.prompt: A company keeps a minimal copy of its core database replicating continuously to a secondary Region, with application servers defined in templates but not running. During a disaster, the servers are launched and scaled up. Which DR strategy is this?
choices: Pilot light
Warm standby
Multi-site active/active
Backup and restore
questions.explanation: Pilot light keeps core data live and replicated while other components are provisioned only when needed. Warm standby runs a scaled-down but fully functional copy.

questions.prompt: A business requires an RTO of a few minutes for a critical application. The company is willing to pay for a scaled-down but fully functional copy of the production environment running in another Region at all times. Which DR strategy is this?
choices: Pilot light
Warm standby
Cold site
Backup and restore
questions.explanation: Warm standby runs a smaller, functional version of production that can be scaled up quickly. Pilot light does not keep the application tier running.

questions.prompt: A global trading platform cannot tolerate more than seconds of downtime and must serve users from two Regions simultaneously. Which DR approach meets this requirement?
choices: Pilot light with a replicated database
Multi-site active/active
Backup and restore from snapshots
Warm standby in a second Region
questions.explanation: Active/active serves traffic from multiple Regions at once, giving near-zero RTO. Warm standby still requires failover and scaling.

questions.prompt: In disaster recovery planning, what does Recovery Point Objective (RPO) measure?
choices: The maximum acceptable time it takes to restore service
The time between scheduled backups and their restore tests
The maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time
The percentage of uptime that is promised in an SLA
questions.explanation: RPO is how much data, expressed as time since the last recovery point, can be lost. RTO is the acceptable downtime.

questions.prompt: A company needs a relational database with cross-Region disaster recovery, typical replication lag under one second, and the ability to promote a secondary Region in about a minute. Which service is BEST?
choices: Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ
Amazon Aurora Global Database
Amazon RDS cross-Region automated backup replication
Amazon DynamoDB global tables
questions.explanation: Aurora Global Database uses storage-level replication with typical lag under a second and supports fast cross-Region failover. DynamoDB is not relational.

questions.prompt: A company wants a multi-Region, multi-active NoSQL database so users in each Region can read and write locally and the application survives a Regional outage. Which solution should be used?
choices: Amazon RDS read replicas in each Region
Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with Multi-AZ
Amazon DynamoDB global tables
Amazon DynamoDB with point-in-time recovery
questions.explanation: Global tables replicate DynamoDB tables across Regions with read and write capability in every replica Region. RDS read replicas are read-only.

questions.prompt: A solutions architect needs to centrally automate and enforce backup schedules and retention for Amazon EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, and Amazon EFS across many accounts. Which service should be used?
choices: AWS Backup with backup plans and AWS Organizations integration
Amazon S3 Lifecycle rules applied to each service's data
AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway with scheduled snapshots
Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policies created in each account
questions.explanation: AWS Backup centrally manages backups across many services and accounts. Data Lifecycle Manager handles only EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs.

questions.prompt: A company must ensure that backups stored in AWS Backup cannot be deleted by anyone, including the root user, for a required retention period. What should be configured?
choices: AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode
An IAM policy denying backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint
S3 Versioning on the backup vault
Vault Lock in governance mode
questions.explanation: Vault Lock in compliance mode makes the vault WORM and cannot be changed or removed once the grace period ends, even by root. Governance mode can be removed by sufficiently privileged users.

questions.prompt: An Amazon RDS database was corrupted by a bad application deployment at 10:42. Automated backups are enabled with a 7-day retention period. What is the BEST way to recover data to just before the corruption?
choices: Fail over the Multi-AZ deployment to the standby
Perform a point-in-time restore to 10:41 into a new DB instance
Restore the most recent manual snapshot over the existing instance
Promote a read replica to primary
questions.explanation: Point-in-time recovery restores to any second within the retention window into a new instance. A Multi-AZ standby or read replica would contain the same corrupted data.

questions.prompt: Which Route 53 routing policy should be used to send all traffic to a primary site and automatically send traffic to a secondary site only when health checks on the primary fail?
choices: Failover routing
Latency-based routing
Weighted routing
Geolocation routing
questions.explanation: Failover routing implements active-passive configurations using health checks. Weighted routing splits traffic by proportion.

questions.prompt: A team wants to send 10 percent of production traffic to a new application version while 90 percent continues to the current version, using DNS. Which Route 53 routing policy should they use?
choices: Multivalue answer routing
Weighted routing
Geoproximity routing
Failover routing
questions.explanation: Weighted routing distributes traffic across records in proportions you specify, which suits canary releases.

questions.prompt: A company wants Route 53 to return up to eight healthy IP addresses for a domain so that clients can choose among them, with unhealthy addresses removed. Which routing policy should be used?
choices: Latency-based routing per Region
Multivalue answer routing
Simple routing with several values
Weighted routing with equal weights
questions.explanation: Multivalue answer routing returns up to eight healthy records chosen at random. Simple routing cannot be associated with health checks.

questions.prompt: A Route 53 health check must determine the health of a private resource that has no public endpoint. What is the recommended approach?
choices: Base the health check on a CloudWatch alarm for a resource metric
Use a calculated health check that has no child checks
Configure the endpoint health check to use HTTPS
Point the health check at the resource's private IP address
questions.explanation: Route 53 health checkers run on the internet and cannot reach private IPs, so you monitor a CloudWatch alarm instead.

questions.prompt: An Application Load Balancer is routing requests to an instance whose application has crashed even though the instance is still running. What should be configured so the ALB stops sending traffic to it?
choices: Connection draining configured with a 300-second timeout
An EC2 status check alarm configured with a reboot action
Cross-zone load balancing enabled on the target group
A target group health check on an app path such as /health
questions.explanation: ALB target group health checks test the application endpoint and stop routing to unhealthy targets. EC2 status checks only test the instance and host.

questions.prompt: An Auto Scaling group behind an ALB is not replacing instances whose application has stopped responding, because EC2 status checks still pass. What should be changed?
choices: Change the group's termination policy to OldestInstance
Enable instance scale-in protection for all of the instances
Enable Elastic Load Balancing health checks on the Auto Scaling group
Increase the health check grace period to 900 seconds
questions.explanation: By default, Auto Scaling uses only EC2 status checks. Turning on ELB health checks makes the group replace instances that fail the load balancer's checks.

questions.prompt: During scale-in, users report dropped connections when instances are removed from behind an Application Load Balancer. What should be adjusted?
choices: The Auto Scaling group default cooldown
The idle timeout on the load balancer
The target group health check interval
The target group deregistration delay
questions.explanation: Deregistration delay (connection draining) lets existing requests finish before a target is removed. The default is 300 seconds.

questions.prompt: An Auto Scaling group spans three Availability Zones. After an AZ outage is resolved, the group has more instances in two AZs than in the third. What will Auto Scaling do?
choices: Rebalance by launching instances in the under-used AZ
Leave the instances unbalanced until a manual change
Live-migrate existing instances into the recovered AZ
Terminate all instances and relaunch them evenly
questions.explanation: Auto Scaling automatically rebalances by launching new instances in the under-represented AZ before terminating others. Instances cannot be moved between AZs.

questions.prompt: A company wants an Auto Scaling group to keep average CPU utilization at about 50 percent without managing alarms manually. Which scaling policy should be used?
choices: Simple scaling with one alarm
Manual scaling by an operator
Target tracking scaling
Scheduled scaling every hour
questions.explanation: Target tracking creates and manages the CloudWatch alarms and adjusts capacity to hold the metric near the target value.

questions.prompt: An application receives a predictable surge every weekday at 9:00 AM, and new instances take 10 minutes to become ready. What is the BEST way to avoid slow responses at the start of the surge?
choices: Reduce the health check grace period on the Auto Scaling group
Add a scheduled scaling action that increases capacity before 9:00 AM
Increase the default cooldown period on the Auto Scaling group
Use a simple scaling policy based on average CPU utilization
questions.explanation: Scheduled scaling adds capacity ahead of a known event, so slow-starting instances are ready in time. Reactive policies respond only after load rises. Predictive scaling is another option.

questions.prompt: Which Auto Scaling feature reduces scale-out latency by keeping a pool of pre-initialized instances in a stopped or running state?
choices: Lifecycle hooks
Capacity Rebalancing
Instance refresh
Warm pools
questions.explanation: Warm pools hold pre-initialized instances that can be moved into service quickly, which helps applications with long boot times.

questions.prompt: Before an instance is terminated by an Auto Scaling group, a script must copy its logs to Amazon S3. Which feature allows this?
choices: A step scaling policy with a scale-in step
A scheduled action on the Auto Scaling group
A lifecycle hook for instance termination
An instance refresh with checkpoints enabled
questions.explanation: Lifecycle hooks put the instance into a wait state (Terminating:Wait) so custom actions can run before termination completes.

questions.prompt: A company needs a highly available NFS file system that multiple Linux EC2 instances in different Availability Zones can mount concurrently. Which service should be used?
choices: Amazon EFS (Regional storage class)
Amazon EBS gp3 with Multi-Attach enabled
Instance store volumes shared over SMB
Amazon S3 mounted through an Elastic IP
questions.explanation: EFS Regional file systems store data across multiple AZs and support thousands of concurrent NFS clients. EBS Multi-Attach works only with io1/io2 within a single AZ.

questions.prompt: What is the durability design of an Amazon EBS volume?
choices: It is replicated across all Availability Zones in a Region
It is not replicated at all
It is replicated across two Regions
It is replicated within a single Availability Zone
questions.explanation: EBS volumes are replicated within their AZ. To survive an AZ failure you need snapshots, which are stored regionally in S3.

questions.prompt: A company must be able to restore an EBS-backed EC2 workload in a second Region during a disaster. What is the MOST straightforward approach?
choices: Rely on the EBS volume's built-in cross-Region replication
Copy EBS snapshots or AMIs to the second Region on a schedule
Move the volumes to the second Region with a cross-Region attachment
Enable EBS Multi-Attach across Regions
questions.explanation: Snapshots and AMIs can be copied cross-Region, for example with AWS Backup or Data Lifecycle Manager. EBS volumes have no cross-Region attachment or replication.

questions.prompt: A company must keep a copy of every new object in an S3 bucket in another Region for disaster recovery. Which feature should be used?
choices: S3 Cross-Region Replication (versioning on both buckets)
S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source bucket
S3 Lifecycle transitions to S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 Same-Region Replication to a second bucket
questions.explanation: CRR asynchronously copies objects to a bucket in another Region and requires versioning on source and destination.

questions.prompt: A company uses S3 Cross-Region Replication and must meet a compliance requirement that 99.99 percent of objects replicate within 15 minutes. What should be enabled?
choices: S3 Replication Time Control (RTC)
S3 Transfer Acceleration on both buckets
S3 Intelligent-Tiering on the destination
S3 Batch Replication run every hour
questions.explanation: S3 RTC is backed by an SLA to replicate 99.99 percent of objects within 15 minutes and provides replication metrics.

questions.prompt: Objects that existed before S3 replication was configured were not copied to the destination bucket. How can they be replicated?
choices: Turn versioning off and on again
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
Enable S3 Replication Time Control
Use S3 Batch Replication
questions.explanation: Live replication only covers new objects; S3 Batch Replication replicates existing objects and those that previously failed.

questions.prompt: Users accidentally delete and overwrite objects in an S3 bucket. What is the simplest way to make them recoverable?
choices: Enable default encryption with SSE-S3
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket
Enable server access logging
questions.explanation: Versioning keeps prior versions and turns deletes into delete markers, so objects can be restored.

questions.prompt: Which Amazon S3 storage class stores data in a single Availability Zone and is appropriate only for re-creatable, infrequently accessed data?
choices: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
questions.explanation: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in one AZ, so the data is lost if that AZ is destroyed. The other classes listed store data across at least three AZs.

questions.prompt: A company wants to route events from several AWS services and SaaS partners to different targets based on content-based rules, without writing polling code. Which service is BEST suited?
choices: Amazon EventBridge
Amazon SQS
AWS Step Functions
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
questions.explanation: EventBridge event buses match events against rules and route them to targets, and they support SaaS partner event sources.

questions.prompt: An EventBridge rule's target Lambda function is sometimes unavailable, and events are dropped after retries. How can the company keep these failed events for reprocessing?
choices: Add a second rule that has exactly the same event pattern
Increase the target Lambda function's timeout to 15 minutes
Configure a dead-letter queue (Amazon SQS) on the rule target
Enable an EventBridge archive and set the replay window to zero
questions.explanation: EventBridge retries delivery and, if a DLQ is configured on the target, sends undeliverable events to the SQS queue for later processing.

questions.prompt: A company needs to re-send events from the past week to a newly fixed consumer after a bug caused incorrect processing. Which EventBridge capability helps?
choices: Event archive and replay
The EventBridge schema registry
Input transformers on the rule
EventBridge API destinations
questions.explanation: EventBridge can archive events matching a pattern and replay them to the bus later.

questions.prompt: A multi-step order workflow must retry failed steps, run a compensating step on failure, and wait for human approval. Which service should coordinate it?
choices: Amazon SNS
Amazon SQS standard queues
AWS Batch
AWS Step Functions
questions.explanation: Step Functions provides built-in Retry and Catch handling, branching, and the wait-for-callback (task token) pattern for human approval.

questions.prompt: A company wants to maximize availability for a stateless web application that runs on EC2 in a single Region. Which design is MOST resilient?
choices: Two large instances in one Availability Zone behind a Network Load Balancer
An Auto Scaling group across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer
One instance with an Elastic IP address and EC2 automatic recovery enabled
A cluster placement group of instances behind an Application Load Balancer
questions.explanation: Distributing instances across multiple AZs behind a load balancer survives instance and AZ failures. A cluster placement group puts instances close together in one AZ.

questions.prompt: An EC2 instance that cannot be placed in an Auto Scaling group must automatically recover onto healthy hardware if the underlying host fails, keeping its instance ID and private IP. What should be configured?
choices: An EBS Multi-Attach volume shared with a standby instance
A Route 53 failover record that points to the instance
A lifecycle hook attached to the stand-alone instance
EC2 automatic recovery triggered by a failed system status check
questions.explanation: EC2 automatic recovery moves the instance to new hardware while retaining its instance ID, private IPs, Elastic IPs, and metadata.

questions.prompt: To reduce the risk of correlated hardware failure for a small group of critical EC2 instances, the instances must each run on distinct underlying racks. Which placement strategy should be used?
choices: Partition placement group with one partition
Dedicated Host affinity
Spread placement group
Cluster placement group
questions.explanation: Spread placement groups put each instance on distinct hardware, with a limit of seven running instances per AZ per group.

questions.prompt: A large HDFS or Cassandra deployment needs instances grouped so that each group is on separate racks and the application is aware of the grouping. Which placement group type fits?
choices: No placement group
Partition placement group
Cluster placement group
Spread placement group
questions.explanation: Partition placement groups divide instances into partitions on separate racks and expose partition information for topology-aware applications.

questions.prompt: Instances in private subnets in three Availability Zones use a single NAT gateway in one AZ. What change BEST improves resilience?
choices: Add a second Elastic IP address to the existing NAT gateway
Replace the NAT gateway with an internet gateway for all subnets
Deploy one NAT gateway per AZ and route each subnet to its local one
Increase the bandwidth that is allocated to the single NAT gateway
questions.explanation: A NAT gateway is redundant within one AZ only. One per AZ removes the cross-AZ dependency if that AZ fails.

questions.prompt: A company relies on a single AWS Direct Connect connection for hybrid connectivity. What is a cost-effective way to add resilience?
choices: Add a second virtual interface on the same connection
Add an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection as a backup path
Enable Direct Connect SiteLink
Increase the port speed of the connection
questions.explanation: A VPN over the internet is a common low-cost backup for Direct Connect. A second VIF on the same physical connection shares the same failure point.

questions.prompt: What is the MOST resilient AWS Direct Connect architecture for critical workloads?
choices: One connection plus an additional public virtual interface
One connection in a link aggregation group with one link
Two connections on the same device at a single location
Separate connections on separate devices at two or more locations
questions.explanation: AWS's maximum resiliency model uses separate connections on separate devices in at least two locations, protecting against device and location failures.

questions.prompt: An application uses Amazon ElastiCache for Redis OSS to store session data, and losing a node must not lose sessions or cause extended downtime. What should be configured?
choices: ElastiCache for Memcached with nodes spread across multiple AZs
Cache nodes launched into one cluster placement group in one AZ
Replicas in multiple AZs with Multi-AZ automatic failover enabled
A single large cache node with daily automatic backups enabled
questions.explanation: Redis OSS replication with Multi-AZ automatic failover promotes a replica when the primary fails. Memcached has no replication, so node data is lost.

questions.prompt: An Aurora MySQL cluster has a writer and two Aurora Replicas. If the writer instance fails, what happens?
choices: The cluster stays read-only until an admin adds a new writer
Aurora fails over to a standby cluster in another Region
Aurora promotes an Aurora Replica to be the new writer
Aurora restores the writer from the latest automated snapshot
questions.explanation: Aurora automatically promotes a replica, based on failover priority tiers, and updates the cluster endpoint.

questions.prompt: How does Amazon Aurora store cluster data to provide durability?
choices: One copy per DB instance kept on instance storage
Three copies spread across two separate Regions
Two copies in one Availability Zone on EBS volumes
Six copies across three AZs in a shared cluster volume
questions.explanation: Aurora storage keeps six copies across three AZs and tolerates loss of two copies for writes and three for reads.

questions.prompt: Applications connecting to an Aurora cluster must automatically connect to the current writer after a failover without code changes. Which endpoint should they use for writes?
choices: A custom endpoint containing all replicas
An instance endpoint of the current writer
The reader endpoint
The cluster endpoint
questions.explanation: The cluster (writer) endpoint always points to the current primary and is updated automatically on failover.

questions.prompt: A company wants an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL deployment with a readable standby and failover typically under 35 seconds. Which option should be chosen?
choices: An RDS Custom DB instance with a manual standby instance
A Multi-AZ DB instance deployment with a single standby
A Single-AZ DB instance with two cross-AZ read replicas
A Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment with two readable standby instances
questions.explanation: Multi-AZ DB clusters have a writer and two readable standbys in three AZs, with faster failover than a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment.

questions.prompt: An RDS for MySQL read replica in another Region must become the primary database during a Regional disaster. What action is required?
choices: Promote the replica to a standalone instance and repoint the app
Nothing; the read replica becomes the primary automatically
Reboot the source DB instance with the failover option
Initiate a Multi-AZ failover on the source DB instance
questions.explanation: RDS read replica promotion is a manual (or scripted) action that makes the replica a standalone writable instance. Cross-Region RDS replicas do not fail over automatically.

questions.prompt: Which type of replication does Amazon RDS use between a source DB instance and its read replicas for MySQL, MariaDB, and PostgreSQL?
choices: Asynchronous replication
Storage-level replication across six copies
Synchronous replication
Snapshot-based replication every 5 minutes
questions.explanation: RDS read replicas use the engine's native asynchronous replication, so replicas can lag the source. Multi-AZ instance standbys use synchronous replication.

questions.prompt: A company wants automated RDS backups to be available in another Region so that it can restore the database there if the primary Region fails. What feature should be enabled?
choices: Performance Insights with long-term retention
A Multi-AZ DB instance deployment
Amazon RDS Proxy with failover targets
Cross-Region automated backup replication
questions.explanation: RDS can replicate snapshots and transaction logs to another Region, enabling point-in-time restore there.

questions.prompt: An application connecting to Amazon RDS opens many short-lived connections from AWS Lambda and suffers errors during database failovers. Which service improves resilience and connection handling?
choices: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached
AWS Global Accelerator
An Application Load Balancer in front of RDS
Amazon RDS Proxy
questions.explanation: RDS Proxy pools connections and can reduce failover times for Aurora and RDS by up to 66 percent by keeping client connections open during failover.

questions.prompt: A DynamoDB table must be restorable to any second within the last 35 days to recover from accidental writes. Which feature provides this?
choices: Global tables in two Regions
DynamoDB Streams with a 24-hour window
On-demand backups taken weekly
Point-in-time recovery (PITR)
questions.explanation: PITR provides continuous backups with restore to any second within the configured recovery period, up to 35 days.

questions.prompt: A company wants to fail over a web application to a static maintenance page hosted in Amazon S3 if the primary ALB becomes unhealthy. Which Route 53 configuration should be used?
choices: Failover routing: ALB as primary, S3 website endpoint as secondary
Simple routing with both the ALB and S3 values in one record
Geolocation routing with a default record that points to S3
Weighted routing with 100 percent to the ALB and 0 percent to S3
questions.explanation: Failover routing sends traffic to the secondary only when the primary is unhealthy. Simple routing cannot use health checks.

questions.prompt: A company wants traffic routed to users based on their country to meet content licensing rules, with a fallback for unmatched locations. Which Route 53 routing policy and setting is needed?
choices: Weighted routing with equal weights
Latency routing with health checks
Geoproximity routing with a negative bias
Geolocation routing with a default record
questions.explanation: Geolocation routing answers by user location, and a default record handles queries from locations with no matching record.

questions.prompt: A Route 53 health check needs to report healthy only if at least two of three underlying endpoint health checks are healthy. What type of health check should be created?
choices: A CloudWatch alarm health check
A calculated health check
A multivalue answer record
An endpoint health check with string matching
questions.explanation: Calculated health checks combine the status of child health checks using a threshold you define.

questions.prompt: An application in two Regions uses Route 53 latency-based records. How can the architect ensure users are not routed to a Region whose application has failed?
choices: Associate health checks with the latency records
Enable DNSSEC signing for the public hosted zone
Lower the TTL of the latency records to 0 seconds
Switch the latency records to simple routing
questions.explanation: With health checks, Route 53 excludes unhealthy records and returns the next-best latency record.

questions.prompt: A company needs a highly available static IP entry point for a multi-Region application, with failover between Regional endpoints in under a minute and without relying on DNS caching. Which service fits BEST?
choices: AWS Global Accelerator
A Network Load Balancer with Elastic IPs
Amazon Route 53 failover routing
Amazon CloudFront with an origin group
questions.explanation: Global Accelerator provides two static anycast IPs and reroutes traffic to healthy endpoints quickly, independent of client DNS caching.

questions.prompt: A CloudFront distribution must automatically serve content from a secondary origin when the primary origin returns 5xx errors. What should be configured?
choices: Lambda@Edge that rewrites the Host header
An origin group with primary and secondary origins
Origin Shield enabled in the secondary Region
Two cache behaviors with the same path pattern
questions.explanation: CloudFront origin failover uses origin groups and retries the secondary origin for specified HTTP status codes.

questions.prompt: A company runs a legacy application on a single EC2 instance and wants it to self-heal automatically if the instance fails, while keeping costs low. Which approach is BEST?
choices: Create a larger instance with termination protection
Purchase a Reserved Instance for the instance type
Attach a second elastic network interface to the instance
Put it in an Auto Scaling group with min, max, and desired of 1
questions.explanation: An Auto Scaling group of one replaces a failed instance automatically, in any configured AZ.

questions.prompt: A company is deploying a new version of its application on an Auto Scaling group and wants instances replaced gradually while keeping a minimum percentage healthy. Which feature should be used?
choices: Lifecycle hooks on the launching transition only
Instance refresh with a minimum healthy percentage
Scheduled scaling actions for each new version
