A warm pool sized to the current desired capacity
questions.explanation: Instance refresh replaces instances in batches based on the launch template version while honoring the minimum healthy percentage.

questions.prompt: An Auto Scaling group uses Spot Instances and wants to proactively replace instances that receive an EC2 rebalance recommendation before they are interrupted. Which feature should be enabled?
choices: Instance scale-in protection
Default cooldown
Capacity Rebalancing
Predictive scaling
questions.explanation: Capacity Rebalancing launches replacement Spot capacity when an instance is at elevated risk of interruption.

questions.prompt: Newly launched instances in an Auto Scaling group are being terminated because they fail ELB health checks while the application is still starting. What should be adjusted?
choices: Reduce the desired capacity of the group
Decrease the target group deregistration delay
Increase the health check grace period
Enable cross-zone load balancing on the ALB
questions.explanation: The grace period delays health check evaluation of new instances so they have time to boot and start the application.

questions.prompt: Which load balancer type should be chosen to handle millions of TCP requests per second with ultra-low latency and static IP addresses per Availability Zone?
choices: Network Load Balancer
Gateway Load Balancer
Classic Load Balancer
Application Load Balancer
questions.explanation: NLB operates at layer 4, scales to millions of requests per second, and supports one static or Elastic IP per AZ.

questions.prompt: What is the default behavior of cross-zone load balancing on an Application Load Balancer?
choices: It is on by default and spreads traffic across targets in all enabled AZs
It is off by default and incurs inter-AZ data transfer charges when on
It applies only to target groups that are using the IP target type
It is off and can only be turned on through an AWS support request
questions.explanation: Cross-zone load balancing is on by default for ALBs (it can be turned off per target group). For NLBs it is off by default.

questions.prompt: A company wants to insert third-party firewall appliances transparently into the traffic path, scaling them and distributing traffic across them. Which load balancer type supports this?
choices: Network Load Balancer
Gateway Load Balancer
Application Load Balancer
Classic Load Balancer
questions.explanation: Gateway Load Balancer uses GENEVE encapsulation to distribute traffic to virtual appliances and health checks them.

questions.prompt: An application stores user session state in local memory on EC2 instances behind an ALB. When instances scale in, users are logged out. What is the MOST resilient fix?
choices: Enable sticky sessions with a longer duration
Move to a larger instance type for the web tier
Store session state in ElastiCache or DynamoDB
Disable scale-in on the Auto Scaling group
questions.explanation: Externalizing state makes the web tier stateless so any instance can serve any request. Sticky sessions still lose state when an instance terminates.

questions.prompt: An application must survive the failure of an Availability Zone while maintaining full capacity of 6 instances. The Region has 3 AZs. What is the minimum number of instances needed to run at all times?
choices: 12 instances, 4 per Availability Zone
7 instances, distributed unevenly
9 instances, 3 per Availability Zone
6 instances, 2 per Availability Zone
questions.explanation: If one AZ fails, the remaining two must hold 6 instances, so each AZ needs 3, for 9 total. With 6 total, losing an AZ leaves only 4.

questions.prompt: A company wants to protect stateful on-premises servers by continuously replicating them at the block level to AWS so that it can recover in AWS within minutes. Which service provides this?
choices: AWS Snowball Edge devices
AWS Transfer Family servers
AWS DataSync scheduled tasks
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
questions.explanation: Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates servers into a low-cost staging area and launches recovery instances in minutes, with RPO of seconds.

questions.prompt: A company must replicate on-premises NFS file data to Amazon EFS on a schedule for disaster recovery. Which service is MOST appropriate?
choices: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration
AWS DataSync
AWS Application Migration Service
questions.explanation: DataSync automates and schedules data transfers between on-premises storage and AWS storage services such as EFS, FSx, and S3.

questions.prompt: A company needs an Amazon EFS file system replicated to another Region for disaster recovery with minimal management. What should be used?
choices: Amazon EFS replication
EBS snapshots of the file system
EFS One Zone storage class
EFS lifecycle management
questions.explanation: EFS replication keeps a read-only replica in another Region or AZ with an RPO typically of minutes; you fail over by deleting the replication configuration.

questions.prompt: A Windows file share on Amazon FSx for Windows File Server must remain available if an Availability Zone fails. Which deployment type should be chosen?
choices: Single-AZ 2 deployment with HDD storage
Single-AZ 1 deployment
Scratch deployment
Multi-AZ deployment
questions.explanation: FSx for Windows Multi-AZ provisions an active and standby file server in two AZs with automatic failover.

questions.prompt: An on-premises application needs low-latency local access to files while the data is durably stored in Amazon S3. Which service fits?
choices: Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive vaults
Amazon EFS mounted over Direct Connect
AWS Storage Gateway S3 File Gateway
AWS Snowcone with local NFS shares
questions.explanation: S3 File Gateway presents NFS/SMB shares on premises with a local cache and stores files as S3 objects.

questions.prompt: A company must move its tape-based backup workflows to AWS without changing the existing backup application. Which option is MOST appropriate?
choices: AWS Storage Gateway S3 File Gateway
AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
AWS DataSync with an on-premises agent
Amazon EBS snapshots stored in Amazon S3
questions.explanation: Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library to existing backup software and stores virtual tapes in S3 and S3 Glacier storage classes.

questions.prompt: A company wants to ensure that messages an SNS topic cannot deliver to a subscriber after retries are not lost. What should be configured?
choices: A FIFO topic with content-based deduplication on
Raw message delivery enabled on the subscription
A message filter policy on the subscription itself
An SQS dead-letter queue set in the subscription redrive policy
questions.explanation: SNS subscriptions can have a redrive policy that sends undeliverable messages to an SQS dead-letter queue.

questions.prompt: A team wants a specific SQS consumer to receive only order messages where the order type is 'priority' from a shared SNS topic. What is the simplest solution?
choices: An SNS subscription filter policy
Consumers deleting unwanted messages
A separate SNS topic for each consumer
An SQS delay queue for each consumer
questions.explanation: Subscription filter policies let a subscriber receive only messages whose attributes (or body) match, reducing custom filtering logic.

questions.prompt: An SQS consumer fleet on EC2 must scale based on the number of messages waiting. Which metric is BEST for the scaling policy?
choices: Average CPUUtilization across the consumer instances
The NumberOfMessagesSent metric reported for the queue
Average NetworkIn reported by the consumer instances
Backlog per instance (visible messages divided by instances)
questions.explanation: AWS recommends target tracking on backlog per instance so capacity matches queue depth and processing rate.

questions.prompt: A Lambda function processes messages from an SQS queue. If one message in a batch fails, the whole batch is retried, causing duplicate processing. What should be done?
choices: Switch the event source from SQS to an SNS trigger
Raise the batch size to the maximum of 10,000 messages
Enable ReportBatchItemFailures and return failed message IDs
Disable the visibility timeout on the source queue
questions.explanation: Partial batch responses let Lambda delete successful messages and only make failed ones visible again.

questions.prompt: An asynchronous Lambda invocation fails after its retries. The team wants the event details and error information sent to another service for analysis. What should be configured?
choices: Reserved concurrency for the function set to zero
An on-failure destination for asynchronous invocations
Provisioned concurrency on the function alias
A larger memory setting for the function
questions.explanation: Lambda destinations send records of failed asynchronous invocations, including error details, to SQS, SNS, Lambda, or EventBridge.

questions.prompt: An architecture uses Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. A consumer application crashes and is restarted 12 hours later. Data must not be lost. What determines whether the data is still available?
choices: The stream's data retention period (24 hours by default)
The consumer's enhanced fan-out registration status
The number of shards provisioned in the stream
The partition key design used by the stream producers
questions.explanation: Records remain in a Kinesis stream for the retention period, so data from 12 hours earlier is still readable with the default 24-hour retention.

questions.prompt: A company runs containers on Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type. How can it ensure the service keeps running if an Availability Zone fails?
choices: Use the host networking mode for all of the service's running tasks
Use a single subnet with a larger CPU and memory task size defined
Give the service subnets in multiple AZs so tasks spread across them
Run all of the service's tasks inside one cluster placement group
questions.explanation: ECS services spread tasks across the AZs of the configured subnets and replace failed tasks automatically.

questions.prompt: An Amazon EKS workload must tolerate AZ failure. Which setup for managed node groups is appropriate?
choices: One node group in a single subnet with very large nodes
Nodes launched into a single cluster placement group
Node groups across multiple AZs with pod topology spread
A single large node that runs all of the pods
questions.explanation: Spreading nodes and pods across AZs lets Kubernetes reschedule pods onto healthy nodes in other AZs.

questions.prompt: A team wants its infrastructure to be reproducible in a recovery Region quickly and consistently. What practice BEST supports this?
choices: Document every console step in a detailed recovery runbook
Define it as code with AWS CloudFormation and deploy via pipelines
Rely on AWS Support to rebuild the resources when needed
Keep screenshots of all resource configurations in a wiki
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as code allows fast, repeatable provisioning in another Region, reducing RTO and human error.

questions.prompt: A company wants to verify that its multi-AZ application actually tolerates the loss of instances and AZ network disruption. Which service lets it run controlled experiments?
choices: AWS Config conformance packs
AWS Trusted Advisor checks
Amazon Inspector assessments
AWS Fault Injection Service
questions.explanation: AWS Fault Injection Service runs chaos engineering experiments such as stopping instances or disrupting AZ connectivity.

questions.prompt: A company wants to coordinate failover of a multi-Region application with readiness checks and routing controls that work even when a Region's control plane is impaired. Which service provides this?
choices: AWS Resilience Hub assessments
Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canaries
AWS Health Dashboard notifications
Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller
questions.explanation: Route 53 ARC provides readiness checks and highly available routing controls that change traffic using data plane operations.

questions.prompt: A company wants to assess applications against defined RTO and RPO targets and get recommendations to improve resilience. Which service should it use?
choices: AWS Cost Explorer
Amazon Detective
AWS Resilience Hub
AWS Compute Optimizer
questions.explanation: Resilience Hub assesses an application's architecture against resiliency policies with RTO/RPO targets and recommends improvements.

questions.prompt: During an Availability Zone impairment, a company wants to quickly shift ALB and NLB traffic away from the affected AZ without changing the application. Which feature helps?
choices: Disabling cross-zone load balancing permanently
Route 53 geolocation routing with a default
S3 Replication Time Control for the targets
Zonal shift in Amazon Application Recovery Controller
questions.explanation: Zonal shift temporarily moves load balancer traffic away from an impaired AZ; zonal autoshift can do it automatically.

questions.prompt: An SQS standard queue sometimes delivers the same message twice. How should the consumer application be designed?
choices: Make message processing idempotent
Set the visibility timeout to 0
Use short polling
Increase the message size
questions.explanation: Standard queues guarantee at-least-once delivery, so consumers should handle duplicates safely.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum size of a single message in Amazon SQS without using the Extended Client Library and S3?
choices: 256 KiB
1 MiB
64 KiB
2 GiB
questions.explanation: Since August 2025, SQS supports message payloads up to 1 MiB (previously 256 KiB); larger payloads can be stored in S3 using the Amazon SQS Extended Client Library.

questions.prompt: Producers send messages to SQS that consumers should not process until 5 minutes later. Which feature handles this simply?
choices: A delivery delay (delay queue) or per-message timer
Increase the queue's visibility timeout to 5 minutes
Enable long polling with a 300-second receive wait
Set the message retention period to just 5 minutes
questions.explanation: Delay queues hide new messages for up to 15 minutes. Visibility timeout only applies after a message is received.

questions.prompt: A tightly coupled monolith fails completely when its reporting module is slow. Which architectural principle would MOST improve resilience?
choices: Move the monolith to a larger instance type
Run the monolith in one AZ close to its users
Add more CPU capacity to the database server
Decouple components with asynchronous messaging
questions.explanation: Loose coupling through queues or events isolates failures and lets components scale independently.

questions.prompt: A company wants to run an Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ broker for an application that requires high availability. What deployment should be chosen?
choices: A single-instance broker inside a cluster placement group
A single-instance broker using a larger instance type
An active/standby broker deployment across two Availability Zones
A single-instance broker with daily automatic backups
questions.explanation: Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ supports active/standby brokers in two AZs with automatic failover.

questions.prompt: A company migrating an application that uses JMS and AMQP messaging wants a managed broker without rewriting messaging code. Which service is BEST?
choices: Amazon SQS
Amazon SNS
Amazon EventBridge
Amazon MQ
questions.explanation: Amazon MQ provides managed ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ brokers that support standard protocols, avoiding code changes. SQS and SNS use AWS APIs.

questions.prompt: A solutions architect wants an Aurora PostgreSQL database to automatically scale capacity during unpredictable spikes while remaining highly available across AZs. Which option fits?
choices: A single provisioned Aurora instance with no replicas
RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ with storage autoscaling
Aurora with a single reader in the same AZ as the writer
Aurora Serverless v2 with a writer and reader in different AZs
questions.explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 scales in fine-grained increments and supports Multi-AZ by adding readers that can be promoted on failover.

questions.prompt: An Aurora cluster has three replicas. The architect wants a specific larger replica to be chosen first during a failover. What should be set?
choices: Move that replica into a secondary AWS Region
Assign that replica the highest failover priority (tier 0)
Enable Backtrack on that specific replica instance
Make that replica the only member of a custom endpoint
questions.explanation: Aurora promotes the replica with the highest priority (lowest tier number); ties are broken by size.

questions.prompt: A team wants to quickly rewind an Aurora MySQL database by a few minutes after an accidental DELETE, without restoring to a new cluster. Which feature allows this?
choices: Database cloning
Aurora Backtrack
Point-in-time restore
Aurora Global Database failover
questions.explanation: Backtrack rewinds an Aurora MySQL cluster in place to a prior time within the backtrack window. PITR creates a new cluster.

questions.prompt: An application on S3 must protect objects from deletion for a fixed regulatory period so that no user, including root, can delete them. Which feature should be used?
choices: MFA Delete with versioning
S3 Object Lock in compliance mode
S3 Object Lock in governance mode
S3 bucket policy denying s3:DeleteObject
questions.explanation: Compliance mode prevents any user, including root, from deleting or overwriting locked object versions until retention expires.

questions.prompt: A company wants periodic, automatic EBS snapshots of tagged volumes with retention rules, at no additional cost beyond snapshot storage. Which service should be used?
choices: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager
Amazon Inspector
AWS DataSync
questions.explanation: Data Lifecycle Manager automates creation, retention, and cross-Region copy of EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs based on tags.

questions.prompt: A large EBS snapshot must be restored and immediately deliver full performance without first-access latency. What should be enabled?
choices: EBS encryption by default in the Region
Elastic Volumes to raise provisioned IOPS
EBS fast snapshot restore in the target AZ
EBS Multi-Attach on the restored volume
questions.explanation: Fast snapshot restore pre-initializes volumes created from the snapshot so they deliver full performance immediately.

questions.prompt: A company accidentally deleted EBS snapshots and wants a safety net to recover deleted snapshots for a set period. Which feature should be configured?
choices: Recycle Bin retention rules for EBS snapshots
Data Lifecycle Manager cross-account copy
EBS snapshot archive tier
S3 Versioning
questions.explanation: Recycle Bin retains deleted EBS snapshots and AMIs for a configured period so they can be restored.

questions.prompt: A web tier of two EC2 instances must remain available if one instance fails, with no single point of failure at the entry point. Which entry point is MOST appropriate?
choices: An Elastic IP address that is remapped manually
A DNS A record that points at one instance
An Elastic Load Balancer spanning both AZs
A NAT gateway that forwards incoming traffic
questions.explanation: ELB is a managed, multi-AZ entry point that routes around failed targets. Manually remapping an Elastic IP adds downtime.

questions.prompt: A company runs a critical stateful application on Amazon EC2 and wants the shortest possible recovery in a second Region with continuous volume replication and an RPO of seconds. Which approach is BEST?
choices: Replicate the servers with AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
Use EBS Multi-Attach to share volumes across Regions
Use S3 Cross-Region Replication for the EBS volumes
Take daily AMIs and copy them to the second Region
questions.explanation: Elastic Disaster Recovery replicates block-level changes continuously and supports cross-Region recovery with RPO in seconds. Daily AMIs give an RPO of up to a day.

questions.prompt: A read-heavy web application on Amazon RDS for MySQL shows high CPU on the DB instance due to repeated identical queries for product catalog data. What is the MOST effective way to improve read performance?
choices: Switch the DB storage to previous-generation magnetic
Increase the automated backup retention period
Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the DB instance
Add ElastiCache to cache frequently read query results
questions.explanation: Caching repeated query results in ElastiCache offloads the database and serves reads in microseconds to milliseconds. Multi-AZ improves availability, not read capacity.

questions.prompt: Which caching strategy loads data into the cache only when the application requests it and finds a cache miss?
choices: Read replica caching
Lazy loading (cache-aside)
Write-through
Write-behind with TTL zero
questions.explanation: With lazy loading, the application checks the cache, and on a miss it reads the database and populates the cache. Write-through updates the cache on every write.

questions.prompt: An application must ensure cached data is never stale after a database update, accepting extra write latency. Which caching strategy should be used?
choices: Lazy loading with a long TTL
Client-side caching only
Lazy loading without TTL
Write-through caching
questions.explanation: Write-through updates the cache whenever the database is written, keeping cached data current at the cost of write latency and possibly caching unread data.

questions.prompt: A team needs an in-memory cache that supports sorted sets for a real-time leaderboard, replication, and persistence. Which option fits BEST?
choices: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis OSS (or Valkey)
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached
Amazon CloudFront with Origin Shield
questions.explanation: Redis OSS and Valkey support rich data structures such as sorted sets, plus replication and persistence. Memcached supports only simple key-value data.

questions.prompt: A company needs a simple, multithreaded, horizontally scalable in-memory cache with no need for persistence or replication. Which engine is MOST suitable?
choices: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis OSS with cluster mode
Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator
Amazon MemoryDB
questions.explanation: Memcached is multithreaded and simple to scale out by adding nodes, and it does not offer persistence or replication.

questions.prompt: A DynamoDB-backed gaming application needs microsecond read latency for hot items without changing much application code. Which service should be added?
choices: DynamoDB Streams
Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with custom code
A DynamoDB global secondary index
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
questions.explanation: DAX is an API-compatible in-memory cache for DynamoDB that delivers microsecond reads with minimal code changes.

questions.prompt: A company needs a durable, Redis-compatible primary database with microsecond reads and single-digit millisecond writes. Which service should be used?
choices: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached
Amazon RDS for MySQL with a large buffer pool
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator
Amazon MemoryDB
questions.explanation: MemoryDB is a durable, in-memory database with a Multi-AZ transaction log, suitable as a primary database. ElastiCache is primarily a cache.

questions.prompt: Users around the world experience slow load times for static images and videos stored in an S3 bucket in us-east-1. What is the MOST effective improvement?
choices: Enable S3 Versioning and S3 Inventory on the bucket
Move the objects to the S3 One Zone-IA storage class
Serve the content through an Amazon CloudFront distribution
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for all of the downloads
questions.explanation: CloudFront caches content at edge locations close to users, reducing latency. Transfer Acceleration mainly speeds long-distance uploads and transfers.

questions.prompt: A CloudFront distribution has a low cache hit ratio because the origin receives many requests that vary only by irrelevant query strings and headers. What should be done?
choices: Add more origins and spread the requests across them
Include only the values the origin needs in the cache key
Lower the default TTL on the distribution to 0 seconds
Disable automatic compression on the distribution
questions.explanation: Removing unnecessary values from the cache key means more requests match existing cached objects, increasing the hit ratio.

questions.prompt: Several CloudFront edge locations in different Regions all fetch the same objects from an origin, increasing origin load. Which feature adds a centralized caching layer to reduce origin requests?
choices: CloudFront Origin Shield
CloudFront Functions
Field-level encryption
Origin access control
questions.explanation: Origin Shield is an additional caching layer in front of the origin that consolidates requests from regional edge caches.

questions.prompt: Users far from us-west-2 upload large files to an S3 bucket in that Region and report slow uploads. What should be enabled to improve upload speed over long distances?
choices: S3 Select
S3 Transfer Acceleration
S3 Cross-Region Replication
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
questions.explanation: Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations over the AWS backbone, improving long-distance transfers.

questions.prompt: An application uploads 5 GB files to Amazon S3 and needs faster, more reliable uploads. What should be used?
choices: S3 Inventory with daily CSV reports
S3 Object Lock in governance mode
A single PUT request for each whole file
Multipart upload with parallel part uploads
questions.explanation: Multipart upload splits objects into parts uploaded in parallel and retried individually. A single PUT is limited to 5 GB and is less resilient; AWS recommends multipart above 100 MB.

questions.prompt: An application must read only a few columns from large CSV objects in S3 without downloading entire objects, and the team wants to query the data with standard SQL in a serverless way. Which service should be used?
choices: AWS Glue DataBrew
Amazon Athena
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
Amazon EMR with HDFS
questions.explanation: Athena runs serverless SQL queries directly against data in S3, paying per data scanned. Converting to columnar Parquet further improves performance.

questions.prompt: Athena queries over a large S3 data lake are slow and expensive. Which change will MOST improve performance?
choices: Convert to partitioned, columnar Apache Parquet files
Move the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
Request a higher request-rate limit for the bucket
Store the data as uncompressed JSON documents
questions.explanation: Columnar, compressed, partitioned data lets Athena scan far less data per query.

questions.prompt: What request rate does Amazon S3 support per partitioned prefix in a bucket?
choices: Unlimited requests with no per-prefix scaling
3,500 writes and 5,500 reads per second, at least
1,000 requests per second of any request type
100 PUT and 300 GET requests per second in total
questions.explanation: S3 supports at least 3,500 write and 5,500 read requests per second per prefix, and you can scale by using more prefixes.

questions.prompt: A database on EC2 needs consistent sub-millisecond latency with up to 256,000 IOPS on a single volume. Which EBS volume type should be used?
choices: Provisioned IOPS SSD io2 Block Express
Throughput Optimized HDD st1
Cold HDD sc1 striped in RAID 0
General Purpose SSD gp3
questions.explanation: io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS per volume with sub-millisecond latency. gp3 and the HDD types support far fewer IOPS per volume.

questions.prompt: A workload on gp2 volumes needs more IOPS without increasing volume size, and the team wants to set IOPS and throughput independently of capacity at lower cost. What should they do?
choices: Migrate to gp3 and provision the needed IOPS and throughput
Change the volumes to Throughput Optimized HDD st1
Add instance store volumes and stripe them with RAID 0
Enlarge the volumes to raise their baseline IOPS
questions.explanation: gp3 lets you provision IOPS and throughput independently of storage size and costs less per GB than gp2.

questions.prompt: A big data workload performs large, sequential reads and writes and needs high throughput at low cost. Which EBS volume type is MOST appropriate?
choices: Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2)
Throughput Optimized HDD (st1)
General Purpose SSD (gp3)
Cold HDD (sc1) for hot data
questions.explanation: st1 is designed for frequently accessed, throughput-intensive sequential workloads such as big data and log processing. sc1 is for colder data.

questions.prompt: Which EBS volume types can be used as boot volumes?
choices: gp2, gp3, io1, io2, and magnetic standard
st1 and sc1 only
Only io2 Block Express
All EBS volume types including st1 and sc1
questions.explanation: HDD volumes st1 and sc1 cannot be boot volumes; SSD types and previous-generation magnetic can.

questions.prompt: An application needs the lowest possible storage latency for temporary scratch data that can be lost if the instance stops. Which storage is BEST?
choices: Amazon EFS One Zone file systems
EBS gp3 volumes at max IOPS
Amazon S3 Express One Zone
EC2 instance store NVMe volumes
questions.explanation: Instance store is physically attached to the host and gives very high IOPS and low latency, but data does not persist across stop or termination.

questions.prompt: An EBS-optimized workload is not reaching the provisioned IOPS of its io2 volume. Monitoring shows the instance is at its EBS bandwidth limit. What should be done?
choices: Increase the provisioned IOPS on the existing io2 volume
Enable EBS encryption on the existing data volume
Move to an instance type with higher dedicated EBS bandwidth
Change the volume type to Throughput Optimized HDD st1
questions.explanation: Instance types have maximum EBS bandwidth and IOPS; if the instance is the bottleneck, a larger or different instance type is needed.

questions.prompt: A machine learning training job reads hundreds of terabytes from S3 and needs a file system with sub-millisecond latency and hundreds of GB/s of throughput, linked to the S3 bucket. Which service should be used?
choices: AWS Storage Gateway S3 File Gateway
Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to the S3 bucket
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
Amazon EFS with Bursting Throughput
questions.explanation: FSx for Lustre is a high-performance parallel file system that integrates with S3 for HPC and ML workloads.

questions.prompt: An Amazon EFS file system has a small amount of stored data but requires consistently high throughput that automatically scales with workload activity. Which throughput mode should be used?
choices: Max I/O performance mode
Bursting throughput
Elastic throughput
Provisioned throughput set to the minimum
questions.explanation: Elastic throughput automatically scales up and down with the workload and is recommended for spiky or unpredictable workloads. Bursting throughput scales with stored size.

questions.prompt: A company needs a fully managed file system for Windows applications that use SMB and Active Directory integration with high performance. Which service fits?
choices: Amazon FSx for Lustre
Amazon EFS with Elastic throughput
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
Amazon S3 with Mountpoint
questions.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server provides native SMB file shares with AD integration. EFS is NFS-based for Linux.

questions.prompt: A company needs shared storage supporting NFS, SMB, and iSCSI with snapshots and data deduplication, to migrate NetApp ONTAP workloads. Which service is BEST?
choices: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
Amazon EFS Regional storage
Amazon FSx for Lustre
Amazon FSx for OpenZFS
questions.explanation: FSx for NetApp ONTAP supports multiprotocol access (NFS, SMB, iSCSI) and ONTAP features such as SnapMirror and deduplication.

questions.prompt: A tightly coupled HPC application needs the lowest network latency and highest packet-per-second performance between instances. Which placement strategy should be used?
choices: No placement group with instances in different AZs
Partition placement group across Regions
Cluster placement group in a single Availability Zone
Spread placement group across three AZs
questions.explanation: Cluster placement groups pack instances close together in one AZ for low-latency, high-throughput networking.

questions.prompt: An HPC application using MPI needs OS-bypass networking to reduce inter-node latency on EC2. Which feature should be used?
choices: AWS Global Accelerator
Elastic Network Interface with multiple IPs
Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA)
VPC Traffic Mirroring
questions.explanation: EFA provides OS-bypass capabilities for MPI and NCCL workloads, giving lower and more consistent latency than standard ENA networking.

questions.prompt: Which EC2 feature provides higher bandwidth, higher packets per second, and lower latency on supported instance types at no extra charge?
choices: Elastic IP addresses on every network interface
Dedicated Hosts with host affinity configured
EC2 Instance Connect with the endpoint enabled
Enhanced networking with the Elastic Network Adapter
questions.explanation: Enhanced networking via ENA uses SR-IOV to deliver higher network performance.

questions.prompt: A memory-intensive in-memory database on EC2 needs a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. Which instance family is MOST appropriate?
choices: Burstable (T family)
Compute optimized (C family)
Storage optimized (I family)
Memory optimized (R family)
questions.explanation: R instances are designed for workloads that process large datasets in memory.

questions.prompt: A batch workload performs CPU-intensive video transcoding and scientific modeling. Which EC2 instance family is MOST appropriate?
choices: Compute optimized (C family)
Memory optimized (R family)
Storage optimized (D family)
Burstable (T family)
questions.explanation: C instances provide high-performance processors for compute-bound applications such as batch processing, encoding, and modeling.

questions.prompt: A NoSQL database on EC2 requires very high random I/O and low-latency local NVMe storage. Which instance family should be chosen?
choices: General purpose (M family)
Accelerated computing (G family)
Storage optimized (I family)
Compute optimized (C family)
questions.explanation: I instances provide high-IOPS local NVMe SSD storage for databases and data-intensive workloads.

questions.prompt: A web application has low average CPU use with occasional short spikes. Which instance family offers a cost-effective baseline with the ability to burst?
choices: Burstable performance (T family)
Memory optimized (X family)
Compute optimized (C family)
Accelerated computing (P family)
questions.explanation: T instances provide baseline CPU with CPU credits for bursting, suiting spiky, low-average workloads.

questions.prompt: A company wants recommendations for right-sizing EC2 instances, EBS volumes, and Lambda memory based on historical utilization metrics. Which service should be used?
choices: AWS Trusted Advisor security checks
AWS Config rules
AWS Compute Optimizer
Amazon Inspector
questions.explanation: Compute Optimizer uses machine learning on CloudWatch metrics to recommend optimal resource configurations for performance and cost.

questions.prompt: A Lambda function's execution is CPU-bound and slow. How can the architect increase the CPU available to the function?
choices: Increase the memory setting, which also raises CPU
Increase the function's reserved concurrency
Increase the function's timeout setting
Attach the function to a VPC with more subnets
questions.explanation: Lambda allocates CPU in proportion to configured memory (up to 10,240 MB, about 6 vCPUs).

questions.prompt: A latency-sensitive API built on AWS Lambda suffers from cold starts during traffic spikes. What should be configured to keep functions initialized and ready?
choices: A dead-letter queue
Reserved concurrency
Provisioned concurrency
A larger ephemeral storage size
questions.explanation: Provisioned concurrency pre-initializes execution environments so requests avoid cold start latency. Reserved concurrency only guarantees or caps concurrency.

questions.prompt: A Java Lambda function has long cold starts because of framework initialization. Which feature can reduce startup latency at low cost without keeping environments always warm?
choices: Lambda SnapStart
Provisioned concurrency set to 1,000
Lambda function URLs
Lambda layers
questions.explanation: SnapStart snapshots the initialized execution environment and resumes from it, reducing cold-start latency for supported runtimes such as Java.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum execution timeout for an AWS Lambda function?
choices: 15 minutes
60 minutes
30 minutes
5 minutes
questions.explanation: Lambda functions can run up to 900 seconds (15 minutes). Longer jobs should use services such as ECS, AWS Batch, or Step Functions.

questions.prompt: A containerized batch job runs for 3 hours and needs no server management. Which compute option is MOST suitable?
choices: AWS Lambda
Amazon API Gateway
Amazon ECS or AWS Batch with AWS Fargate
AWS App Runner with a 15-minute limit
questions.explanation: Fargate runs containers serverlessly without the 15-minute limit that applies to Lambda.

questions.prompt: A REST API on Amazon API Gateway returns the same responses for many repeated GET requests, and backend latency is high. What feature reduces latency for these requests?
choices: Switch to a private API endpoint
Enable API Gateway stage caching
Enable usage plans with API keys
Enable mutual TLS on the custom domain
questions.explanation: API Gateway REST API caching stores responses for a TTL so repeated requests do not reach the backend.

questions.prompt: A company needs a low-latency, lower-cost API in front of Lambda functions and only needs JWT authorizers and basic routing. Which API Gateway option is BEST?
choices: HTTP API
REST API with edge-optimized endpoint
WebSocket API
REST API with private endpoint
questions.explanation: HTTP APIs are designed for low latency and lower cost, with native JWT authorizers, but have fewer features than REST APIs.

questions.prompt: A DynamoDB table experiences throttling on a few partition keys even though total provisioned capacity is not exceeded. What is the MOST likely cause and fix?
choices: A hot partition; redesign for high-cardinality partition keys
The table needs an additional local secondary index
Point-in-time recovery is consuming the table's capacity
The items have too many attributes and must be trimmed
questions.explanation: Throughput is spread across partitions, so concentrating traffic on a few keys causes throttling. High-cardinality keys or write sharding spread the load.

questions.prompt: A new application has unpredictable DynamoDB traffic that can spike from zero to thousands of requests per second. Which capacity mode is MOST appropriate?
choices: Provisioned capacity with reserved capacity
Provisioned capacity with no auto scaling
Provisioned capacity with a fixed 5 RCUs
On-demand capacity mode
questions.explanation: On-demand mode scales instantly to accommodate traffic without capacity planning, ideal for unpredictable workloads.

questions.prompt: An application needs to query a DynamoDB table by an attribute other than the table's partition key, and the index must be created after the table exists. What should be used?
choices: A global secondary index
A Scan with a filter expression
A local secondary index
DynamoDB Streams
questions.explanation: GSIs can use a different partition key and can be added at any time. LSIs must be created with the table and share its partition key.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum size of a single item in Amazon DynamoDB?
choices: 16 MB
400 KB
1 MB
64 KB
questions.explanation: DynamoDB items can be up to 400 KB including attribute names and values; larger objects are typically stored in S3 with a pointer in DynamoDB.

questions.prompt: A DynamoDB-based application must trigger processing in near real time whenever items are inserted or updated. Which feature should be used?
choices: DynamoDB Streams with an AWS Lambda trigger
DynamoDB Time to Live on new items
A global secondary index on a status flag
Scheduled DynamoDB on-demand backups
questions.explanation: DynamoDB Streams captures item-level changes, and Lambda can process them as they occur.

questions.prompt: A DynamoDB table must support a read pattern where eventual consistency is acceptable and cost per read should be minimized. Which read type should be used?
choices: Scan operations with parallel segments
Transactional reads
Strongly consistent reads
Eventually consistent reads
questions.explanation: Eventually consistent reads consume half the read capacity of strongly consistent reads (one RCU covers two 4 KB eventually consistent reads per second).

questions.prompt: A company needs to ingest clickstream data from thousands of producers in real time and have multiple applications process the same records with replay capability. Which service is BEST?
choices: Amazon SQS standard queue
AWS Batch
Amazon SNS standard topic
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
questions.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams stores ordered records per shard for the retention period, allowing multiple consumers and replay. SQS messages are deleted once processed.

questions.prompt: A company wants to load streaming data into Amazon S3 and Amazon Redshift with automatic batching, compression, and format conversion, without managing consumers. Which service should be used?
choices: AWS DataSync
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with custom KCL consumers
Amazon Data Firehose
Amazon SQS FIFO
questions.explanation: Amazon Data Firehose (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose) is fully managed and delivers streaming data to destinations like S3, Redshift, and OpenSearch with buffering and transformation.

questions.prompt: Each shard in a provisioned Kinesis data stream supports what write throughput?
choices: 10 MB per second or 10,000 records per second
2 MB per second or 2,000 records per second
1 MB per second or 1,000 records per second
512 KB per second or 500 records per second
questions.explanation: A shard supports 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s for writes and 2 MB/s for reads shared across consumers (or 2 MB/s per consumer with enhanced fan-out).

questions.prompt: Multiple consumer applications reading the same Kinesis data stream are hitting read throughput limits and latency. What should be enabled so each consumer gets dedicated throughput?
choices: Enhanced fan-out
Extended data retention
Server-side encryption
On-demand capacity mode only
questions.explanation: Enhanced fan-out gives each registered consumer its own 2 MB/s per shard with push delivery, reducing contention and latency.

questions.prompt: A company wants a fully managed Apache Kafka service for an existing Kafka-based streaming application. Which service should be chosen?
choices: Amazon SNS FIFO topics
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon MSK
Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ
questions.explanation: Amazon MSK runs Apache Kafka clusters with compatible APIs, so existing Kafka applications can migrate without code changes.

questions.prompt: A reporting workload runs complex analytical SQL queries over petabytes of structured data and needs columnar storage and massively parallel processing. Which service is MOST appropriate?
choices: Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon Redshift
Amazon ElastiCache
Amazon RDS for MySQL
questions.explanation: Redshift is a columnar, MPP data warehouse built for analytical queries at scale. RDS is optimized for OLTP.

questions.prompt: Analysts want to query data in an S3 data lake directly from Amazon Redshift without loading it into Redshift tables. Which feature should be used?
choices: AWS Glue DataBrew
Amazon Redshift Spectrum
Redshift RA3 managed storage only
Redshift concurrency scaling
questions.explanation: Redshift Spectrum queries data in S3 using external tables, joining it with data stored in the cluster.

questions.prompt: A Redshift cluster experiences slow queries when many users run queries at the same time during business hours. Which feature adds capacity automatically for concurrent read queries?
choices: Elastic resize to a single node
Redshift Spectrum
Concurrency scaling
Automatic table vacuum
questions.explanation: Concurrency scaling adds transient cluster capacity to handle bursts of concurrent queries.

questions.prompt: An application performs full-text search with relevance ranking and log analytics over large volumes of data. Which service should be used?
choices: Amazon DynamoDB Scan operations
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with LIKE queries
Amazon Neptune
questions.explanation: OpenSearch Service provides managed search and analytics with full-text search, aggregations, and dashboards.

questions.prompt: A social network needs to run queries on highly connected data, such as friends-of-friends recommendations, with low latency. Which database is MOST appropriate?
choices: Amazon Neptune
Amazon DocumentDB
Amazon Timestream
Amazon Redshift
questions.explanation: Neptune is a managed graph database optimized for traversing relationships. Relational joins for deep relationships perform poorly.

questions.prompt: An IoT application stores large volumes of time-stamped sensor measurements and needs fast time-series queries using a purpose-built time-series engine. Which database is BEST?
choices: Amazon DocumentDB
Amazon RDS for MariaDB
Amazon Timestream
Amazon Neptune
questions.explanation: Timestream is AWS's purpose-built time-series database with built-in time-series functions; new customers use Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB, since Timestream for LiveAnalytics is closed to new customers.

questions.prompt: A company wants a managed document database that is compatible with MongoDB APIs and scales reads with up to 15 replicas. Which service should be chosen?
choices: Amazon Keyspaces for Apache Cassandra
Amazon Neptune Serverless graph clusters
Amazon DynamoDB with global tables
Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
questions.explanation: DocumentDB offers MongoDB-compatible APIs with a storage architecture similar to Aurora that supports up to 15 replicas.

questions.prompt: A company runs Apache Cassandra workloads and wants a serverless, managed service that supports CQL. Which service fits?
choices: Amazon MemoryDB Multi-Region
Amazon Neptune Analytics graphs
Amazon DocumentDB elastic clusters
Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra)
questions.explanation: Keyspaces is a serverless, Cassandra-compatible database that supports CQL.

questions.prompt: A reporting workload slows down the primary Aurora writer during business hours. What is the BEST way to improve performance without affecting writes?
choices: Add a Multi-AZ standby instance for the cluster writer
Enable Backtrack on the Aurora cluster for reporting
Increase the cluster's automated backup retention period
Add Aurora Replicas and use the reader endpoint for reports
questions.explanation: Aurora Replicas share the cluster volume and serve read traffic; the reader endpoint load-balances connections across them.

questions.prompt: An Aurora cluster has replicas of different sizes. The team wants analytics queries to use only the two largest replicas, while application reads use the others. What should be configured?
choices: Aurora Global Database secondary clusters
Route 53 weighted records pointing to instance IPs
Custom endpoints that group the specific replicas
Two separate cluster endpoints for the same cluster
questions.explanation: Aurora custom endpoints let you load-balance connections across a chosen subset of instances.

questions.prompt: Read traffic on Aurora fluctuates widely during the day. How can the number of Aurora Replicas adjust automatically?
choices: A Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment instead of Aurora
Aurora Auto Scaling for replicas with a target tracking metric
Storage autoscaling configured on the cluster volume
A higher max_connections value in the parameter group
questions.explanation: Aurora Auto Scaling adds or removes Aurora Replicas based on a target tracking policy.

questions.prompt: An RDS for PostgreSQL database is reaching the I/O limits of its General Purpose storage during peak transactions. Which change MOST directly increases I/O performance?
choices: Enable Performance Insights on the instance
Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the instance
Move the storage to Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1 or io2)
Add a cross-Region read replica for the instance
questions.explanation: Provisioned IOPS storage delivers consistent, high I/O for I/O-intensive OLTP workloads. Multi-AZ does not increase primary I/O capacity.

questions.prompt: A team needs to identify which SQL statements and wait events are causing load on an Amazon RDS database. Which tool should it use?
choices: AWS X-Ray service maps
Amazon VPC Flow Logs with Athena
Amazon RDS Performance Insights
AWS Trusted Advisor checks
questions.explanation: Performance Insights visualizes database load by SQL, wait, user, and host to pinpoint bottlenecks.

questions.prompt: A team needs a full-size copy of a 20 TB production Aurora database for load testing, created in minutes without duplicating storage up front. Which feature should be used?
choices: Restore from the latest snapshot
Export the cluster to Amazon S3
Aurora fast database cloning
Create a cross-Region read replica
questions.explanation: Aurora cloning uses copy-on-write so the clone shares storage with the source and is created quickly; only changed pages consume new storage.

questions.prompt: A company needs to choose a database for a high-volume shopping cart with simple key-value access patterns and single-digit millisecond latency at any scale. Which service is BEST?
choices: Amazon Neptune
Amazon RDS for Oracle
Amazon Redshift
Amazon DynamoDB
questions.explanation: DynamoDB is a key-value and document database that provides consistent single-digit millisecond performance at virtually any scale.

questions.prompt: Users across several continents access an application in one Region over TCP and UDP. The company wants to improve performance by routing traffic over the AWS global network from the nearest edge. Which service should be used?
choices: Route 53 simple routing
A VPC peering connection
AWS Global Accelerator
Amazon CloudFront with static caching
questions.explanation: Global Accelerator onboards user traffic at the nearest edge location and uses the AWS backbone, improving performance for TCP and UDP applications.

questions.prompt: When should a solutions architect choose AWS Global Accelerator over Amazon CloudFront?
choices: When running Lambda@Edge functions on every viewer request
For TCP/UDP apps needing static anycast IPs and fast failover
When caching static website images at many edge locations
When serving video on demand that is protected by signed URLs
questions.explanation: CloudFront caches HTTP(S) content at the edge; Global Accelerator proxies TCP/UDP traffic to Regional endpoints without caching.

questions.prompt: A company wants Route 53 to send users to the AWS Region that gives them the lowest network latency. Which routing policy should be used?
choices: Weighted routing
Simple routing
Geolocation routing
Latency-based routing
questions.explanation: Latency-based routing uses latency measurements between users and Regions to route to the lowest-latency Region. Geolocation routes by location, not latency.

questions.prompt: A company wants to shift more traffic to a Region by expanding the geographic area it serves. Which Route 53 routing policy supports a bias value to do this?
choices: Latency routing
Geoproximity routing
Multivalue answer routing
Failover routing
questions.explanation: Geoproximity routing routes based on resource location and lets you expand or shrink an area with a bias value.

questions.prompt: EC2 instances in a private subnet download large amounts of data from Amazon S3 in the same Region through a NAT gateway, which limits throughput and adds charges. What is the BEST solution?
choices: Add an S3 gateway endpoint to the private route tables
Route the private subnets directly to an internet gateway
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source bucket
Add a second NAT gateway in the same public subnet
questions.explanation: A gateway endpoint gives private, direct access to S3 over the AWS network without NAT gateway processing charges or bottlenecks.

questions.prompt: A company needs consistent, high-bandwidth, low-latency connectivity between its data center and AWS for transferring large datasets daily. Which option is BEST?
choices: AWS Client VPN
AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the internet
AWS Direct Connect
VPC peering
questions.explanation: Direct Connect provides dedicated private connectivity with consistent network performance, unlike internet-based VPNs.

questions.prompt: A company's Site-to-Site VPN connections use standard tunnels, each limited to about 1.25 Gbps. How can the company increase aggregate VPN bandwidth to AWS?
choices: Enable jumbo frames on the virtual private gateway
Use a transit gateway with ECMP across several VPN connections
Add more static route entries to the VPC's route tables
Increase the MTU of each of the VPN tunnels to 9001 bytes
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway supports equal-cost multi-path routing across multiple VPN tunnels to scale bandwidth.

questions.prompt: A company has 50 VPCs that need to communicate with each other and with on-premises networks. Which approach scales BEST and simplifies routing?
choices: Create a full mesh of VPC peering connections
Use interface VPC endpoints between each VPC pair
Connect everything to an AWS Transit Gateway
Deploy a NAT gateway in every VPC for routing
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway acts as a regional hub, avoiding the large number of peering connections a full mesh needs; peering is also non-transitive.

questions.prompt: Traffic between EC2 instances in different Availability Zones has higher latency than desired for a chatty, latency-sensitive microservice pair. What is the BEST improvement?
choices: Create a VPC peering connection between the two instances' subnets
Assign Elastic IP addresses to both of the communicating instances
Place both instances in the same AZ, ideally a cluster placement group
Route all the traffic between them through an internet gateway
questions.explanation: Keeping chatty components in the same AZ reduces network latency and inter-AZ data transfer, though it trades off some resilience.

questions.prompt: A media company serves large video files through CloudFront and wants to run lightweight header manipulation and URL rewrites on every viewer request at the lowest latency and cost. Which option is BEST?
choices: Lambda@Edge on origin requests
AWS Lambda with a function URL
An Application Load Balancer listener rule
CloudFront Functions
questions.explanation: CloudFront Functions run lightweight JavaScript at edge locations with sub-millisecond startup, ideal for simple viewer request and response changes.

questions.prompt: A CloudFront use case requires network calls to external services and access to the request body during processing at the edge. Which option should be used?
choices: Lambda@Edge
CloudFront signed cookies
Origin Shield
CloudFront Functions
questions.explanation: Lambda@Edge supports network access, longer execution, and request body access; CloudFront Functions do not.

questions.prompt: A dynamic website on an ALB serves personalized pages that cannot be cached. How can CloudFront still improve performance for global users?
choices: Set a one-year TTL on all of the personalized dynamic pages
Put CloudFront in front of the ALB to accelerate dynamic requests
Move the ALB's targets into a cluster placement group
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for the load balancer
questions.explanation: CloudFront accelerates dynamic content through optimized TCP connections, connection reuse to the origin, and the AWS backbone, even with caching disabled.

questions.prompt: An application stores many small objects and must deliver single-digit millisecond data access for latency-sensitive workloads co-located with compute in one Availability Zone. Which S3 storage class is designed for this?
choices: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 Standard-IA
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
S3 Express One Zone
questions.explanation: S3 Express One Zone uses directory buckets in a single AZ to deliver consistent single-digit millisecond access, up to 10x faster than S3 Standard.

questions.prompt: Archived data in S3 must be retrievable in milliseconds when occasionally accessed, about once a quarter. Which storage class meets this at low cost?
choices: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 One Zone-IA
questions.explanation: Glacier Instant Retrieval offers millisecond retrieval for rarely accessed data. Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive take minutes to hours.

questions.prompt: Which retrieval option for S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval typically returns data within 1 to 5 minutes?
choices: Standard retrieval
Expedited retrieval
Instant retrieval
Bulk retrieval
questions.explanation: Expedited retrievals typically complete in 1 to 5 minutes; Standard takes 3 to 5 hours and Bulk 5 to 12 hours.

questions.prompt: An image-processing pipeline must create thumbnails as soon as images are uploaded to S3, scaling automatically with upload volume and without servers. Which design is BEST?
choices: Use AWS Batch with a fixed compute environment polling S3
Use S3 Inventory reports to find new objects
Run a cron job on EC2 that lists the bucket every hour
Use S3 event notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function
questions.explanation: S3 events trigger Lambda per object, scaling automatically with uploads and avoiding idle servers.

questions.prompt: A company wants to run a containerized web application with automatic scaling, load balancing, and TLS without managing clusters or servers. Which service requires the LEAST operational effort?
choices: Amazon EC2 with Docker installed
Amazon EKS with self-managed nodes
Amazon ECS on EC2 with a capacity provider
AWS App Runner
questions.explanation: App Runner builds and runs containerized web apps with built-in load balancing, scaling, and TLS, with no infrastructure to manage.

questions.prompt: A large-scale batch workload of thousands of independent jobs needs automatic provisioning of compute based on job queue requirements. Which service is MOST appropriate?
choices: Amazon SQS FIFO
Amazon EventBridge Scheduler
AWS Step Functions Express Workflows
AWS Batch
questions.explanation: AWS Batch manages job queues and dynamically provisions EC2 or Fargate compute for batch jobs.

questions.prompt: A company needs to process a large dataset with Apache Spark and Hadoop without managing the cluster software installation. Which service fits BEST?
choices: Amazon Athena
Amazon EMR
AWS Glue Data Catalog
Amazon Redshift
questions.explanation: EMR is a managed big data platform for frameworks like Spark, Hadoop, Hive, and Presto.

questions.prompt: A company wants a serverless ETL service to transform data in S3 and catalog schemas for query by Athena. Which service should be used?
choices: Amazon EMR on EC2
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
AWS Glue
AWS DataSync
questions.explanation: Glue provides serverless Spark-based ETL jobs and a Data Catalog with crawlers that Athena uses for table definitions.

questions.prompt: A machine learning inference workload needs GPU acceleration on EC2. Which instance family is MOST appropriate?
choices: Burstable performance (T family)
Accelerated computing (G or P family)
Compute optimized (C family)
Memory optimized (R family)
questions.explanation: G and P instances provide NVIDIA GPUs for graphics, ML training, and inference. Inf instances with AWS Inferentia are another option.

questions.prompt: A company wants better price performance for a Linux web tier and its software supports ARM. Which EC2 option should it evaluate?
choices: Dedicated Hosts with x86 processors
Instances powered by AWS Graviton processors
Previous-generation M4 instances
Instances that use only instance store
questions.explanation: Graviton-based instances offer up to 40 percent better price performance than comparable x86 instances for many workloads.

questions.prompt: A website needs to scale to handle a sudden 10x traffic increase for a flash sale with minimal load on the origin servers. Most pages are static. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Cache static content in CloudFront and offload it from the origin
Increase the Auto Scaling group maximum to 1,000 and remove caching
Use a single large EC2 instance
Store pages on EBS io2 volumes
questions.explanation: Serving cached static pages from edge locations absorbs most of the spike, so only dynamic requests reach the origin.

questions.prompt: An Auto Scaling group must scale based on application request load per instance behind an ALB. Which predefined target tracking metric is BEST?
choices: ALBRequestCountPerTarget
NetworkPacketsIn
DiskReadOps
ASGAverageNetworkOut
questions.explanation: ALBRequestCountPerTarget tracks requests per target, scaling capacity directly with request load.

questions.prompt: A company's traffic has daily and weekly patterns, and it wants EC2 capacity provisioned ahead of forecasted demand using machine learning. Which feature should be used?
choices: Step scaling with a single step
Predictive scaling
Manual scaling
Simple scaling
questions.explanation: Predictive scaling analyzes historical load to forecast demand and schedules capacity in advance.

questions.prompt: A DynamoDB table needs to automatically delete session items 24 hours after creation without consuming write capacity. Which feature should be used?
choices: Time to Live (TTL) on an expiry timestamp attribute
DynamoDB Streams with an event filtering rule
A global secondary index with a date sort key
A scheduled Lambda function that runs DeleteItem
questions.explanation: TTL deletes expired items automatically in the background at no write cost.

questions.prompt: An application's DynamoDB queries frequently need a different sort order on the same partition key, and the table is being designed now. Which index allows this with strongly consistent reads?
choices: A sparse global secondary index on the table
A local secondary index defined at table creation
A global secondary index on the same keys
The DAX item cache in front of the table
questions.explanation: LSIs share the table's partition key with an alternate sort key and support strongly consistent reads. GSIs support only eventual consistency.

questions.prompt: A gaming company has steady, predictable DynamoDB traffic with occasional moderate increases. Which capacity configuration gives good performance at the lowest cost?
choices: Provisioned capacity with no auto scaling set to peak
DAX instead of table capacity
Provisioned capacity with DynamoDB auto scaling
On-demand capacity mode
questions.explanation: For predictable traffic, provisioned capacity with auto scaling tracks usage and is generally cheaper than on-demand.

questions.prompt: An analytics team needs sub-second dashboards and interactive BI visualizations over data in Redshift and S3. Which service should be used for visualization?
choices: Amazon Managed Grafana for SQL ETL
Amazon Athena
AWS Glue
Amazon QuickSight
questions.explanation: QuickSight (now Amazon Quick Sight, part of Amazon Quick Suite) is a serverless BI service that uses the SPICE in-memory engine for fast interactive dashboards.

questions.prompt: A company processes streaming data in real time with SQL or Apache Flink to compute rolling metrics over a Kinesis data stream. Which service should be used?
choices: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
Amazon EMR Serverless with batch jobs only
AWS Glue crawlers
Amazon Athena
questions.explanation: Managed Service for Apache Flink (formerly Kinesis Data Analytics) runs Flink applications for real-time stream processing.

questions.prompt: A Kinesis data stream's traffic is unpredictable and the team does not want to manage shard counts. What should be done?
choices: Use enhanced fan-out
Increase the retention period to 365 days
Use provisioned mode with a fixed single shard
Use on-demand capacity mode for the stream
questions.explanation: On-demand mode automatically scales stream capacity with throughput, removing shard management.

questions.prompt: An application needs to decouple producers from consumers while processing up to nearly unlimited messages per second without ordering requirements. Which SQS queue type should be used?
choices: FIFO queue with a single message group
Standard queue
Delay queue with FIFO enabled
FIFO queue without high throughput mode
questions.explanation: Standard queues support nearly unlimited throughput. FIFO queues have throughput limits (higher with high throughput mode).

questions.prompt: Consumers of an SQS queue make many empty ReceiveMessage calls, increasing cost and latency. What should be configured?
choices: A visibility timeout of 12 hours on the queue
Long polling with a wait time of up to 20 seconds
Short polling with a receive wait time of 0
A delivery delay of 15 minutes on the queue
questions.explanation: Long polling waits for messages to arrive, reducing empty responses and false empty receives.

questions.prompt: A serverless workflow orchestrates high-volume, short-duration event processing of up to 5 minutes per execution at the lowest cost. Which Step Functions workflow type should be used?
choices: Activity tasks with EC2 workers
Express Workflows
Map state with Standard Workflows only
Standard Workflows
questions.explanation: Express Workflows are designed for high-volume, short-lived (up to 5 minutes) executions and are billed by executions and duration.

questions.prompt: A three-tier application has a stateless web tier on EC2 and a relational database. The company expects rapid, unpredictable growth. Which design BEST supports scaling performance?
choices: ALB with an Auto Scaling web tier, Aurora Replicas, and ElastiCache
Web servers in a spread placement group with an instance store DB
One web instance with an Elastic IP and a Single-AZ RDS database
One large EC2 instance running both the web server and database
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling at the web tier, read scaling at the database, and caching hot data together let each layer scale independently.

questions.prompt: An application in VPC A must connect to a database in VPC B in the same Region over an existing VPC peering connection. The database must accept traffic only from the application instances, whose IP addresses change frequently. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Reference the peer VPC's application security group in the database security group
Add each application instance's current private IP address to the database security group
Allow the entire CIDR range of VPC A in the database subnet's network ACL only
Route the traffic through a NAT gateway and allow the NAT gateway's Elastic IP
questions.explanation: For VPC peering connections in the same Region, a security group rule can reference a security group in the peer VPC, so access follows the instances regardless of IP changes. Allowing the whole CIDR is broader than required.

questions.prompt: A user in Account A must copy objects from a bucket in Account B into a bucket in Account A in a single operation, using permissions from both accounts at once. Which approach meets this requirement?
choices: Make the Account B bucket public for the duration of the copy
Grant the user access in a bucket policy on the Account B bucket
Create IAM users for the person in both accounts and switch between them
Have the user assume a role in Account B for the entire copy operation
questions.explanation: With a resource-based policy, the principal keeps its own identity-based permissions while also being granted access to the other account's resource. Assuming a role replaces the user's original permissions with the role's permissions.

questions.prompt: An IAM role has the AdministratorAccess managed policy attached, and a permissions boundary that allows only Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB actions. Which actions can the role perform?
choices: No actions, because the two policies conflict
All actions, because AdministratorAccess overrides the boundary
Only S3 and DynamoDB actions allowed by both policies
Only IAM actions, because boundaries restrict only the other AWS services
questions.explanation: Effective permissions are the intersection of the identity-based policy and the permissions boundary. The boundary does not grant permissions but limits the maximum the identity policy can grant.

questions.prompt: An S3 bucket must be accessible only to requests that originate from the company's corporate office public IP address range over the internet. Which bucket policy condition key should be used?
choices: aws:SourceVpce
aws:SecureTransport
aws:PrincipalOrgID
aws:SourceIp
questions.explanation: aws:SourceIp matches the requester's public IP address range. aws:SourceVpce applies to requests that arrive through a specific VPC endpoint, which carry private source addresses instead.

questions.prompt: A customer managed KMS key must be usable for decryption only when requests come through Amazon S3, not when principals call AWS KMS directly. Which key policy condition key enforces this?
choices: kms:ViaService
kms:EncryptionAlgorithm
kms:GrantIsForAWSResource
aws:SourceIp
questions.explanation: The kms:ViaService condition limits use of a KMS key to requests made on the principal's behalf by specified AWS services, such as s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com.

questions.prompt: A Lambda function is attached to private subnets in a VPC so it can reach an RDS database. It must also call a third-party API on the internet. What should a solutions architect configure?
choices: Assign an Elastic IP address directly to the Lambda function
Route internet-bound traffic through a NAT gateway in a public subnet
Move the function into a public subnet that has a route to an internet gateway
Create an interface VPC endpoint for the third-party API's domain
questions.explanation: Lambda network interfaces in a VPC never receive public IP addresses, even in public subnets, so internet access requires a NAT gateway. Interface endpoints work only for AWS and PrivateLink services.

questions.prompt: Administrators must SSH into EC2 instances in private subnets that have no public IP addresses, without deploying bastion hosts or installing extra agents, using standard SSH clients. Which feature should be used?
choices: A Gateway Load Balancer in front of the instances
A NAT gateway for inbound SSH connections
An EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint in the VPC
An internet gateway with a public subnet route
questions.explanation: EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint provides private SSH and RDP connectivity to instances without public IPs or bastion hosts, controlled by IAM and security groups. A NAT gateway only supports outbound connections.

questions.prompt: A company is adding HTTPS to an Application Load Balancer in eu-west-1 using AWS Certificate Manager. In which Region must the certificate be requested or imported?
choices: Any Region, because ACM certificates are global
The Region of the company's Route 53 hosted zone
us-east-1, regardless of the load balancer's Region
eu-west-1, the same Region as the load balancer
questions.explanation: ACM certificates are regional resources and must be in the same Region as the ALB that uses them. Only CloudFront requires certificates from us-east-1.

questions.prompt: A media company must stop viewers in two countries from accessing content served through its CloudFront distribution, with the LEAST additional cost and configuration. What should it use?
choices: CloudFront geographic restrictions
An AWS WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule
Route 53 geolocation routing to a null record
Security group rules on the origin servers
questions.explanation: CloudFront's built-in geographic restrictions allow or block countries at no extra charge. AWS WAF geo match rules also work but add WAF charges and configuration, and origin security groups cannot see viewer countries.

questions.prompt: A mobile game lets players browse a public leaderboard stored in Amazon S3 without signing in, and grants more access after sign-in. Which solution provides temporary, limited AWS credentials to guest players?
choices: An Amazon Cognito user pool with no identity pool configured at all
A Cognito identity pool that allows unauthenticated identities
Long-term IAM access keys embedded securely in the game client code
A public S3 bucket policy that allows all actions
questions.explanation: Cognito identity pools can issue temporary credentials to unauthenticated (guest) identities through a separate, tightly scoped IAM role. User pools handle sign-in but do not issue AWS credentials on their own.

questions.prompt: A security team wants to prevent anyone in an account from making Amazon EBS snapshots publicly accessible in a Region. What is the simplest control?
choices: Enable S3 Block Public Access for the account
Attach a permissions boundary to every IAM user and role
Enable block public access for EBS snapshots
Enable EBS encryption by default
questions.explanation: Block public access for EBS snapshots is an account-level, per-Region setting that prevents public sharing of snapshots. S3 Block Public Access applies only to S3 buckets and objects.

questions.prompt: Instances in private subnets read and write an Amazon DynamoDB table. Traffic must not traverse the internet, and the company wants the lowest-cost solution. What should a solutions architect configure?
choices: An internet gateway with restrictive security groups and network ACLs
An AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to DynamoDB
A NAT gateway in each Availability Zone
A DynamoDB gateway VPC endpoint in the route tables
questions.explanation: DynamoDB, like S3, supports gateway VPC endpoints, which have no hourly or data processing charges and keep traffic on the AWS network. NAT gateways send traffic toward public endpoints and add charges.

questions.prompt: A security team wants to be alerted automatically when an account shows an unusual spike in the rate of write API calls or API errors compared with its normal baseline. Which feature should be enabled?
choices: CloudTrail Insights on the trail
AWS Config conformance packs
VPC Flow Logs for every subnet in the account
S3 server access logging
questions.explanation: CloudTrail Insights analyzes management events to detect unusual API call rates and error rates and records Insights events when activity deviates from the baseline.

questions.prompt: A compliance standard requires that objects in Amazon S3 be protected with two independent layers of server-side encryption. Which option meets this requirement with the LEAST effort?
choices: Server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) only
Dual-layer server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (DSSE-KMS)
S3 Object Lock in governance mode
Server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)
questions.explanation: DSSE-KMS applies two layers of encryption to objects on the server side using KMS keys, designed for standards that require multilayer encryption. Object Lock controls deletion, not encryption.

questions.prompt: An application in Account B must read a secret stored in AWS Secrets Manager in Account A. The secret is currently encrypted with the AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager. What must be done to allow cross-account access?
choices: Only add Account B to the secret's resource policy and leave the key unchanged
Enable automatic rotation on the secret
Use a customer managed KMS key, and allow Account B in its key policy and the secret policy
Copy the AWS managed key to Account B and use it there for decryption
questions.explanation: Cross-account access to a secret requires a resource policy on the secret and a customer managed KMS key whose key policy allows the other account. The key policy of an AWS managed key cannot be changed.

questions.prompt: A Network Load Balancer spans two Availability Zones, but one AZ has many more registered targets than the other, and targets in the smaller AZ are overloaded. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Enable sticky sessions on the listener
Replace the NLB with a Classic Load Balancer
Increase the target group deregistration delay for all of the targets
Enable cross-zone load balancing on the Network Load Balancer
questions.explanation: Cross-zone load balancing is off by default for NLBs, so each load balancer node sends traffic only to targets in its own AZ. Turning it on spreads traffic evenly across all registered targets.

questions.prompt: A company must keep backups of its DynamoDB tables in a second Region to recover from a Regional disaster, with centrally managed schedules and retention. Which solution meets this requirement?
choices: An AWS Backup plan for the tables with a cross-Region copy rule
DynamoDB TTL with a long expiry period
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) clusters in the second Region
DynamoDB on-demand backups, which are automatically stored in every Region
questions.explanation: AWS Backup can schedule DynamoDB backups and copy recovery points to a vault in another Region. On-demand DynamoDB backups stay in the source Region, and DAX is a cache, not a backup.

questions.prompt: An application connects to an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance using the IP address it resolved when it first started. After a failover, the application cannot reconnect. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Assign an Elastic IP address to the DB instance
Connect by the endpoint DNS name and re-resolve it on reconnect
Disable Multi-AZ to keep the IP address stable
Point the application at the standby instance's private IP address permanently
questions.explanation: During a Multi-AZ failover, RDS updates the endpoint's DNS record to point to the new primary. Applications must use the endpoint name and avoid caching the old IP address.

questions.prompt: A company uses Amazon ElastiCache for Redis OSS in us-east-1 and needs a replicated copy in another Region that can be promoted quickly during a Regional outage. Which feature should be used?
choices: ElastiCache Multi-AZ with automatic failover in the same Region
DynamoDB global tables in front of the cache
ElastiCache Global Datastore
Redis AOF persistence to an EBS volume
questions.explanation: Global Datastore replicates a Redis OSS or Valkey cluster to secondary Regions with low latency, and a secondary can be promoted to primary. Multi-AZ protects only within one Region.

questions.prompt: An application in several Regions reads and writes objects in replicated S3 buckets. It needs a single global endpoint for S3 requests and the ability to shift traffic away from a Region's bucket during an outage. Which feature should be used?
choices: S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoints
S3 Same-Region Replication rules
S3 Access Points created separately in each Region with VPC-only network origin
S3 Multi-Region Access Points with failover controls
