questions.explanation: Multi-Region Access Points provide one global endpoint that routes requests to buckets in multiple Regions, and failover controls let you set buckets active or passive to shift traffic.

questions.prompt: A new Amazon ECS service deployment keeps failing because the new tasks never pass health checks, and the service gets stuck. The team wants failed deployments to roll back automatically. What should be enabled?
choices: The ECS deployment circuit breaker with rollback
Fargate Spot as the capacity provider
ECS Service Auto Scaling with a target tracking scaling policy
A longer container stop timeout
questions.explanation: The deployment circuit breaker detects deployments that cannot reach a steady state and, with rollback enabled, returns the service to the last completed deployment.

questions.prompt: A company must deploy the same baseline infrastructure, defined in one CloudFormation template, to many accounts and to a disaster recovery Region, and keep it consistent. Which feature should be used?
choices: CloudFormation change sets in a single account
AWS CloudFormation StackSets
AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments
CloudFormation drift detection only
questions.explanation: StackSets deploy and update stacks across multiple accounts and Regions from a single template and operation, which supports consistent multi-Region recovery environments.

questions.prompt: Route 53 alias records with failover routing point to Application Load Balancers in two Regions. Traffic must move to the secondary Region if the primary ALB has no healthy targets, without creating separate health checks. What should be configured?
choices: Lower the TTL of the alias records to 0
Enable cross-zone load balancing on both ALBs
Set Evaluate Target Health to Yes on the alias records
Use simple routing with both ALBs listed in a single record
questions.explanation: With Evaluate Target Health enabled, an alias record to an ALB inherits the health of the load balancer's targets, so Route 53 fails over when the primary has no healthy targets.

questions.prompt: A Lambda function triggered by a high-volume event source writes to a relational database that fails when more than 50 connections are open. How can the architect stop the function from overwhelming the database?
choices: Increase the function's memory setting
Increase the function's timeout to the 15-minute maximum
Enable provisioned concurrency on the function
Set reserved concurrency on the function
questions.explanation: Reserved concurrency sets a maximum number of concurrent instances for a function, limiting downstream connections. Provisioned concurrency pre-initializes environments but does not cap scaling.

questions.prompt: A cost-sensitive team runs an Aurora MySQL cluster with only a single writer instance and no Aurora Replicas. What happens if that instance fails?
choices: Aurora creates a new DB instance, which is slower than a replica failover
Aurora switches the cluster to read-only mode permanently
Aurora promotes a standby in another Region automatically
The cluster's data is lost because no replica holds a copy of the data
questions.explanation: Without replicas, Aurora recreates the writer instance, which typically takes longer than promotion. Data is safe in the cluster volume, which keeps six copies across three AZs; adding replicas in other AZs enables fast failover.

questions.prompt: A public API on Amazon API Gateway must protect its backend from sudden traffic surges that could cause failures, by rejecting excess requests. What should be configured?
choices: Mutual TLS on the custom domain name
Stage or method throttling limits on the API
An API Gateway resource policy allowing all IPs
A longer integration timeout for the backend
questions.explanation: API Gateway throttling sets steady-state rate and burst limits; requests above them receive 429 Too Many Requests, protecting downstream services.

questions.prompt: A Lambda function is invoked asynchronously by Amazon S3 event notifications. If the function returns an error, how does Lambda handle the event by default?
choices: It discards the event immediately
It retries indefinitely until the function succeeds
It retries the invocation up to two more times
It sends the event back to S3 to resend later
questions.explanation: For asynchronous invocations, Lambda retries failed events twice by default, with delays between attempts. A dead-letter queue or on-failure destination can capture events that still fail.

questions.prompt: A Kinesis Data Streams consumer built with the Kinesis Client Library (KCL) restarts after a crash. How can it continue from where it left off instead of reprocessing the whole stream?
choices: Kinesis deletes records as soon as they are read
The producers automatically resend all of their records after a consumer restart
Each consumer keeps checkpoints only in instance memory
KCL resumes from checkpoints stored in a DynamoDB lease table
questions.explanation: KCL uses a DynamoDB lease table to track shard ownership and checkpoints, so a restarted worker resumes after the last checkpointed record.

questions.prompt: An order-processing system uses an SQS FIFO queue and needs much higher throughput than the default FIFO limits, while keeping ordering per customer. What should a solutions architect do?
choices: Enable FIFO high throughput mode and use many message group IDs
Switch to a standard queue and keep the same consumers
Increase the queue's message retention period
Use one message group ID for all messages so ordering is fully global
questions.explanation: High throughput mode raises FIFO throughput, which scales across message group IDs. Ordering is kept within each group, so using the customer ID as the group ID preserves per-customer order.

questions.prompt: An application downloads very large objects from Amazon S3 and wants to speed up transfers by retrieving parts of each object in parallel. What should it use?
choices: S3 Inventory reports
Byte-range fetches in parallel
S3 Object Lock retention modes
S3 Lifecycle transition rules to faster tiers
questions.explanation: Byte-range fetches let clients request specific ranges of an object concurrently, improving throughput and allowing retries of only the failed parts.

questions.prompt: A Lambda function must download and unpack a 3 GB archive for processing during each invocation, but it runs out of local disk space. What is the simplest fix?
choices: Increase the function's timeout to 15 minutes
Attach a 10 GB Amazon EBS volume to the function
Increase the function's ephemeral storage (/tmp)
Enable provisioned concurrency
questions.explanation: Lambda ephemeral storage in /tmp can be configured from 512 MB up to 10,240 MB. Lambda functions cannot attach EBS volumes.

questions.prompt: Several Lambda functions need to load the same multi-gigabyte machine learning model files and share them, and the files are too large to package with the function. Which solution fits BEST?
choices: Store the files in Lambda environment variables
Store the files in the function's /tmp of one instance
Package the files in a Lambda layer
Mount an Amazon EFS file system to the functions
questions.explanation: Lambda can mount Amazon EFS file systems for shared, persistent storage that is larger than deployment packages or layers allow. Layers have size limits, and /tmp is not shared between execution environments.

questions.prompt: A Redshift dashboard repeatedly runs the same complex aggregation query over large tables, and each run is slow. Which feature MOST improves performance for this repeated query?
choices: A materialized view of the query results
An ElastiCache cluster in front of Redshift
Redshift Spectrum external tables
Increasing the WLM query timeout for the dashboard queue
questions.explanation: Materialized views store precomputed results that can be refreshed incrementally, so repeated complex queries return much faster. Spectrum is for querying data in S3, not for speeding up repeated aggregations.

questions.prompt: Producers write to a Kinesis data stream with several shards, but one shard is throttled while the others are nearly idle. Most records use the same partition key. What should be done?
choices: Switch consumers to the Kinesis Client Library
Use a high-cardinality partition key for the records
Increase the stream's data retention period
Enable enhanced fan-out for every consumer
questions.explanation: The partition key determines which shard receives each record, so a low-cardinality key creates a hot shard. Enhanced fan-out improves read throughput, not write distribution.

questions.prompt: A REST API on Amazon API Gateway is called almost entirely by applications running on EC2 in the same AWS Region. Which endpoint type gives the lowest latency for these clients?
choices: A CloudFront distribution in front of an edge-optimized endpoint
An edge-optimized API endpoint
A Regional API endpoint
A private API with no VPC endpoint
questions.explanation: Regional endpoints are designed for clients in the same Region and avoid the extra hop through CloudFront that edge-optimized endpoints add. Edge-optimized endpoints help geographically distributed clients.

questions.prompt: A company is migrating Linux applications that use an on-premises ZFS-based NFS file server and need sub-millisecond latency with features such as snapshots and clones. Which service fits BEST?
choices: Amazon EBS Multi-Attach volumes
Amazon S3 with S3 File Gateway
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
Amazon FSx for OpenZFS
questions.explanation: FSx for OpenZFS provides fully managed OpenZFS file systems accessible over NFS with low latency, snapshots and clones. FSx for Windows File Server targets SMB-based Windows workloads.

questions.prompt: Users in Europe experience slow reads from an Amazon RDS for MySQL database in us-east-1, while all writes can stay in us-east-1. What is the MOST appropriate way to reduce read latency for European users?
choices: Add a cross-Region read replica in Europe for European reads
Enable Multi-AZ on the primary DB instance
Increase the primary instance size
Enable RDS Performance Insights on the primary DB instance
questions.explanation: A cross-Region read replica places a copy of the data close to European users for low-latency reads. Multi-AZ improves availability, not read latency, and its standby does not serve reads.

questions.prompt: An ElastiCache for Redis OSS cluster with a single shard has reached the write capacity of its primary node. How can the cluster scale write throughput?
choices: Add more read replicas to the existing shard in other AZs
Use cluster mode enabled with multiple shards
Enable Multi-AZ automatic failover
Switch to a larger EBS volume
questions.explanation: With cluster mode enabled, data is partitioned across multiple shards, each with its own primary, so writes scale horizontally. Read replicas only add read capacity.

questions.prompt: An application on a single EC2 instance needs more throughput and IOPS than one EBS volume can provide, and the application handles data redundancy itself. Which approach can increase performance?
choices: Configure several EBS volumes as a RAID 1 mirror
Convert the volumes to Cold HDD (sc1)
Stripe several EBS volumes in RAID 0
Enable EBS fast snapshot restore
questions.explanation: RAID 0 striping combines the IOPS and throughput of multiple volumes. RAID 1 mirrors data for redundancy and does not increase write performance.

questions.prompt: A team wants to run a containerized machine learning inference service on Amazon ECS that requires GPUs. Which launch option should be used?
choices: ECS on AWS Fargate with a GPU task definition
AWS Lambda with container images
AWS App Runner with GPU instances
ECS on EC2 with GPU instances
questions.explanation: AWS Fargate does not provide GPUs, so GPU workloads on ECS run on EC2 container instances from accelerated computing families. Lambda and App Runner also do not offer GPUs.

questions.prompt: Analysts want to run complex queries on a full copy of a large production DynamoDB table every week without consuming the table's read capacity. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?
choices: Export the table to S3 and query the export with Athena
Add a global secondary index for each query
Run a parallel Scan of the table each week
Add a DAX cluster and run all of the analytic queries through it
questions.explanation: Exporting a table to S3 uses point-in-time recovery data and does not consume read capacity; Athena can then query the export. Scans consume large amounts of read capacity.

questions.prompt: An Amazon OpenSearch Service domain keeps 12 months of logs on hot data nodes, but logs older than 30 days are searched only occasionally. Which change reduces cost the MOST while keeping the data searchable?
choices: Add more hot data nodes
Move older indexes to UltraWarm or cold storage
Enable Multi-AZ with standby on the domain for all data
Increase the EBS volume size on each node
questions.explanation: UltraWarm and cold storage keep read-only data searchable at much lower cost than hot nodes by storing it in Amazon S3-backed tiers.

questions.prompt: A bucket uses S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Much of the data is not accessed for six months or longer, and waiting up to 12 hours to retrieve it would be acceptable. How can storage costs be reduced further automatically?
choices: Move all objects to S3 Standard
Enable S3 Versioning and noncurrent version transitions on the bucket
Activate the optional archive access tiers
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
questions.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering's archive tiers are opt-in; once activated, objects not accessed for the configured periods move automatically to lower-cost archive tiers.

questions.prompt: An Amazon ECR repository has accumulated thousands of old container image versions, and storage costs keep rising. Which solution reduces cost with the LEAST ongoing effort?
choices: Manually delete images every month
Enable image scanning on push
Replicate the repository to a cheaper Region and delete the original
Create an ECR lifecycle policy to expire old images
questions.explanation: ECR lifecycle policies automatically expire images based on rules such as age or count, for example keeping only the latest 20 images.

questions.prompt: A new Amazon RDS database will start with 100 GB of data, but its growth is hard to predict. The company does not want to pay for a large amount of unused storage up front. What should be configured?
choices: RDS storage autoscaling with a maximum threshold
Create a read replica to hold the extra data as it grows
Provision 5 TB of storage at creation time
Use Provisioned IOPS at the maximum level
questions.explanation: Storage autoscaling increases allocated storage automatically when free space runs low, up to a maximum you set, so you do not need to overprovision storage.

questions.prompt: An Amazon EFS file system stores project files that are opened only a few times a year after projects close, but must remain in the same file system. Which option reduces cost the MOST?
choices: Create EFS replication to another Region
Lifecycle management to the EFS Archive storage class
Switch the file system to Provisioned throughput
Copy the files to EBS Provisioned IOPS volumes
questions.explanation: EFS Archive is designed for data accessed a few times a year or less and costs less than EFS Infrequent Access; lifecycle policies move files there automatically.

questions.prompt: A team runs analytics queries for a few hours each week, with long idle periods in between. It wants to use Amazon Redshift without paying for an always-on cluster. Which option is MOST cost-effective?
choices: A provisioned Redshift cluster with RA3 nodes running 24/7
Redshift Reserved Nodes for three years
Amazon Redshift Serverless
A large provisioned cluster with concurrency scaling
questions.explanation: Redshift Serverless charges for compute capacity only while queries run, so intermittent workloads avoid paying for idle provisioned clusters.

questions.prompt: Two VPCs in the same Region need private connectivity to each other, and no other networks will be connected. Which option is MOST cost-effective?
choices: AWS Direct Connect gateway
AWS Site-to-Site VPN between the VPCs
AWS Transit Gateway
VPC peering
questions.explanation: VPC peering has no hourly charge, and you pay only for data transfer. Transit Gateway adds per-attachment hourly and data processing charges, which make sense only when connecting many networks.

questions.prompt: A Lambda function starts an external job and then loops and sleeps for up to 10 minutes while waiting for it to finish, paying for idle duration. Which redesign reduces cost?
choices: A Step Functions Standard workflow with Wait states
Move the loop to a larger EC2 instance
Increase the function's memory to finish faster
Enable provisioned concurrency for the function
questions.explanation: A Standard workflow is billed per state transition, not for time spent waiting, so a Wait state avoids paying for idle Lambda duration.

questions.prompt: A company runs non-urgent nightly AWS Glue ETL jobs whose start and finish times can vary. Which option reduces cost for these jobs?
choices: Convert each job into a Glue crawler
Use the AWS Glue Flex execution class
Increase the number of workers for each job so it finishes sooner
Run the jobs as Glue streaming jobs
questions.explanation: The Flex execution class runs non-urgent jobs on spare capacity at a lower price, accepting variable start and run times.
